title.raw: 卷54 游雅 高閭 Volume 54: You Ya, Gao Lu

sentences.zh: 游雅 高閭

translations.literal: You Ya, Gao Lu
translations.idiomatic: You Ya and Gao Lu

sentences.zh: 游雅，字伯度，小名黃頭，廣平任人也。

translations.literal: You Ya, styled Bodu, childhood name Huangtou, was a man of Ren in Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: You Ya, whose courtesy name was Bodu and childhood name was Huangtou, was a native of Ren in Guangping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 少好學，有高才。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and had great talent.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was devoted to study and possessed exceptional talent.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，與勃海高允等俱知名，徵拜中書博士、東宮內侍長，遷著作郎。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Shizu, together with Gao Yun of Bohai and others he was equally renowned; summoned and appointed Central Secretariat Doctor and Eastern Palace Inner Attendant Chief, transferred to Drafting Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Taiwu, he was as well known as Gao Yun of Bohai and others. He was summoned and appointed Central Secretariat Doctor and Chief Inner Attendant of the Eastern Palace, then promoted to Drafting Clerk.

sentences.zh: 使劉義隆，授散騎侍郎，賜爵廣平子，加建威將軍。

translations.literal: Sent on mission to Liu Yilong, granted Attendant Cavalier and Regular, bestowed title Marquis of Guangping, given additional title General Who Establishes Prestige.
translations.idiomatic: On an embassy to Liu Yilong, he was granted the post of Attendant Cavalier and Regular, given the title Marquis of Guangping, and additionally appointed General Who Establishes Prestige.

sentences.zh: 稍遷太子少傅，領禁兵，進爵為侯，加建義將軍。

translations.literal: Gradually transferred to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, commanding palace guards, advanced in noble rank to Marquis, given additional title General Who Establishes Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and placed in command of the palace guard. His noble rank was raised to Marquis, and he was further appointed General Who Establishes Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 受詔與中書侍郎胡方回等改定律制。

translations.literal: Received edict together with Central Secretariat Attendant Hu Fanghui and others to revise laws and institutions.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he joined Central Secretariat Attendant Hu Fanghui and others in revising the laws and regulations.

sentences.zh: 出為散騎常侍、平南將軍、東雍州刺史，假梁郡公。

translations.literal: Sent out as Attendant Cavalier and Regular, General Who Pacifies the South, Governor of Eastern Yong Province, acting Duke of Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as Attendant Cavalier and Regular, General Who Pacifies the South, and Governor of Eastern Yong Province, with the provisional title Duke of Liang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 在任廉白，甚有惠政。

translations.literal: In office he was incorrupt and upright, with very effective benevolent governance.
translations.idiomatic: During his tenure he was upright and honest, and his administration brought genuine benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 徵為祕書監，委以國史之任。

translations.literal: Summoned as Director of the Secretariat, entrusted with the charge of national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Director of the Secretariat and entrusted with responsibility for the dynastic history.

sentences.zh: 不勤著述，竟無所成。

translations.literal: He was not diligent in writing, and in the end achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He was lax about his writing duties and ultimately produced nothing of note.

sentences.zh: 詔雅為太華殿賦，文多不載。

translations.literal: An edict had Ya compose the "Rhapsody on the Taihua Hall"; most of the text is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Ya to compose a rhapsody on the Taihua Hall, but most of the piece was not preserved in the record.

sentences.zh: 雅性剛戇，好自矜誕，陵獵人物。

translations.literal: Ya by nature was rigid and blunt, fond of self-praise and boastfulness, trampling on people.
translations.idiomatic: Ya was by nature blunt and obstinate, given to self-aggrandizement and contempt for others.

sentences.zh: 高允重雅文學，而雅輕薄允才，允性柔寬，不以為恨。

translations.literal: Gao Yun valued Ya's literary learning, but Ya slighted Yun's talent; Yun by nature was gentle and broad-minded and did not regard it as resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun held Ya's literary accomplishments in esteem, but Ya looked down on Yun's abilities. Yun was gentle and magnanimous by nature and did not resent it.

sentences.zh: 允將婚于邢氏，雅勸允娶于其族，允不從。

translations.literal: When Yun was about to marry into the Xing clan, Ya urged Yun to marry within his own clan; Yun did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun was preparing to marry a woman of the Xing clan, Ya urged him to take a wife from the You family instead, but Yun refused.

sentences.zh: 雅曰：「人貴河間邢，不勝廣平游。

translations.literal: Ya said: "People esteem the Xing of Hejian — they cannot surpass the You of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Ya said, "People may honor the Xing of Hejian, but they cannot outrank the You of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 人自棄伯度，我自敬黃頭。

translations.literal: People may reject Bodu themselves; I myself honor Huangtou.
translations.idiomatic: Others may reject Bodu, but I myself honor Huangtou.

sentences.zh: 」貴己賤人，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His exalting himself and belittling others were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His habit of exalting himself and belittling others was all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 允著徵士頌，殊為重雅，事在允傳。

translations.literal: Yun composed "Praise of Reclusive Scholars," greatly esteeming Ya; the matter is recorded in Yun's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun composed "Praise of Reclusive Scholars," in which he held Ya in high regard; the account appears in Yun's biography.

sentences.zh: 雅因論議長短，忿儒者陳奇，遂陷奇至族，議者深責之。

translations.literal: Because of a dispute over comparative merits, Ya, angered at the scholar Chen Qi, brought Qi down and extended punishment to his whole clan; commentators deeply blamed him for it.
translations.idiomatic: In a debate over comparative merits, Ya grew angry at the scholar Chen Qi, had him condemned, and extended the punishment to his entire clan. Commentators strongly condemned him for this.

sentences.zh: 和平二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of the Heping era.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Heping era.

sentences.zh: 贈相州刺史，諡曰宣侯。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Governor of Xiang Province; posthumous title Xuan Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Governor of Xiang Province, with the posthumous name Marquis Xuan.

sentences.zh: 子僧奴，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Sengnu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sengnu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 卒，子雙鳳襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Shuangfeng inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Shuangfeng succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 雅弟恒，子曇護。

translations.literal: Ya's younger brother Heng; his son Tanhu.
translations.idiomatic: Ya's younger brother was Heng; Heng's son was Tanhu.

sentences.zh: 太和中，為中散，遷典寺令。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, he served as Palace Attendant, transferred to Director of the Bureau of Monasteries.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he served as Palace Attendant and was later promoted to Director of the Bureau of Monasteries.

sentences.zh: 後慰勞仇池，為賊所害。

translations.literal: Later, while going to comfort and reward Qiuchi, he was killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while on a mission to confer rewards upon Qiuchi, he was killed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 贈肆州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Governor of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Governor of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 高閭，字閻士，漁陽雍奴人。

translations.literal: Gao Lu, styled Yanshi, was a man of Yongnu in Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu, whose courtesy name was Yanshi, was a native of Yongnu in Yuyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 五世祖原，晉安北軍司、上谷太守、關中侯，有碑在薊中。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Yuan was Jin General of the Army for Pacifying the North, Administrator of Shanggu, and Marquis of Guanzhong; a stele to him stands in Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Yuan served Jin as General of the Army for Pacifying the North, Administrator of Shanggu, and Marquis of Guanzhong; a commemorative stele to him still stood in Ji.

sentences.zh: 祖雅，少有令名，州別駕。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ya had a fine reputation from youth and served as Provincial Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ya enjoyed an excellent reputation from youth and served as Provincial Attendant.

sentences.zh: 父洪，字季願，陳留王從事中郎。

translations.literal: His father Hong, styled Jiyuan, was Attendant of the Affairs Section under the Prince of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hong, whose courtesy name was Jiyuan, served the Prince of Chenliu as Attendant of the Affairs Section.

sentences.zh: 閭貴，乃贈寧朔將軍、幽州刺史、固安貞子。

translations.literal: When Lu became honored, Hong was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the North, Governor of You Province, and Viscount of Gu'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu rose to prominence, his father was posthumously granted the titles General Who Pacifies the North, Governor of You Province, and Viscount of Gu'an.

sentences.zh: 閭早孤，少好學，博綜經史，文才儁偉，下筆成章。

translations.literal: Lu lost his father early, loved learning from youth, mastered the classics and histories comprehensively, had outstanding literary talent, and wrote finished compositions at a stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Lu was orphaned early. From youth he loved learning, mastered the classics and histories, possessed outstanding literary talent, and could compose finished prose at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 本名驢，司徒崔浩見而奇之，乃改為閭而字焉。

translations.literal: His original name was Donkey; Minister of Works Cui Hao saw him and considered him extraordinary, and so changed it to Lu and gave him a courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: His original given name was Donkey. Minister of Works Cui Hao, struck by his talent, changed it to Lu and gave him the courtesy name Yanshi.

sentences.zh: 真君九年，徵拜中書博士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of the Zhenjun era, summoned and appointed Central Secretariat Doctor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Zhenjun era he was summoned and appointed Central Secretariat Doctor.

sentences.zh: 和平末，遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Heping era, transferred to Central Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Heping era he was promoted to Central Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩，乙渾擅權，內外危懼。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wencheng died, Yue Hun seized power arbitrarily, and inside and outside the court were filled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wencheng died, Yue Hun seized power, and fear spread throughout the court and the realm.

sentences.zh: 文明太后臨朝，誅渾，引閭與中書令高允入於禁內，參決大政，賜爵安樂子。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming took charge of the court, executed Hun, summoned Lu and Central Secretariat Director Gao Yun into the inner palace to participate in deciding great affairs, and bestowed the title Viscount of Anle.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming assumed regency, executed Yue Hun, and summoned Lu and Central Secretariat Director Gao Yun into the inner palace to help decide major affairs of state. Lu was granted the title Viscount of Anle.

sentences.zh: 加南中郎將，與鎮南大將軍尉元南赴徐州，閭先入彭城，收管籥，元表閭以本官領東徐州刺史，與張讜對鎮團城。

translations.literal: Given additional title General of the Southern Palace Gentlemen; together with General Who Guards the South Wei Yuan he went south to Xuzhou. Lu entered Pengcheng first, took charge of the keys, Yuan memorialized that Lu with his existing office should also serve as Governor of Eastern Xu Province, and together with Zhang Dan he jointly garrisoned Tuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed General of the Southern Palace Gentlemen and marched south to Xuzhou with General Who Guards the South Wei Yuan. Lu entered Pengcheng first and took control of the city gates. Yuan memorialized that Lu, retaining his existing rank, should also serve as Governor of Eastern Xu Province, and Lu garrisoned Tuancheng jointly with Zhang Dan.

sentences.zh: 後還京城，以功進爵為侯，加昭武將軍。

translations.literal: Later he returned to the capital; for his achievements his noble rank was advanced to Marquis, and he was given the additional title General Who Displays Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: When he later returned to the capital, his noble rank was raised to Marquis for his achievements, and he was further appointed General Who Displays Martiality.

sentences.zh: 顯祖傳位，徙御崇光宮，閭上表頌曰：

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzu transferred the throne and moved to dwell at Chongguang Palace, Lu submitted a memorial of praise, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianwen abdicated and moved to Chongguang Palace, Lu submitted a memorial of praise that read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞創制改物者，[1]應天之聖君；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that those who create institutions and transform things are sage rulers who respond to Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that those who create new institutions and transform the world are sage rulers who respond to Heaven;

sentences.zh: 齷齪順常者，守文之庸主。

translations.literal: those who are narrow-minded and follow convention are mediocre rulers who merely preserve inherited forms.
translations.idiomatic: while those who are narrow-minded and cling to convention are mediocre rulers who merely preserve what they inherit.

sentences.zh: 故五帝異規而化興，三王殊禮而致治，用能憲章萬祀，垂範百王，歷葉所以挹其遺風，後君所以酌其軌度。

translations.literal: Thus the Five Emperors had different standards yet civilization flourished; the Three Kings had different rites yet good governance was achieved. By this they could serve as models for ten thousand generations and provide standards for a hundred kings — successive ages drink from their surviving influence, and later rulers measure themselves against their norms.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Emperors followed different standards yet civilization flourished; the Three Kings observed different rites yet good order was achieved. In this way they became models for ten thousand generations and standards for a hundred kings — later ages draw from their surviving influence, and succeeding rulers take their norms as measure.

sentences.zh: 伏惟太上皇帝，道光二儀，明齊日月，至德潛通，武功四暢。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that the Retired Emperor's virtue illumines the two principles, his brilliance equals sun and moon, his supreme virtue secretly pervades all, and his martial achievements extend in the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that the Retired Emperor's virtue illumines heaven and earth, his brilliance equals the sun and moon, his supreme virtue quietly pervades all things, and his martial achievements extend in every direction.

sentences.zh: 霜威南被，則淮徐來同；

translations.literal: When his frost-like authority spread southward, Huai and Xu came to submit;
translations.idiomatic: When his frost-like authority spread southward, the Huai and Xu regions came to submit;

sentences.zh: 齊斧北斷，則獫狁覆斃。

translations.literal: when his imperial axe struck northward, the Xianyun were overthrown and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: when his imperial axe struck northward, the Xianyun were overthrown and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 西摧三危之酋，東引肅慎之貢，荒遐款塞，九有宅心。

translations.literal: In the west he crushed the chieftains of Sanwei; in the east he received tribute from Sushen. Distant lands came in submission, and the Nine Domains found their heart's home.
translations.idiomatic: In the west he crushed the chieftains of Sanwei; in the east he received tribute from Sushen. Remote lands came in submission, and the Nine Domains found their rightful center.

sentences.zh: 於是從容閑覽，希心玄奧，尚鼎湖之奇風，崇巢由之高潔，疇咨熙載，亮采羣后，爰挹大位，傳祚聖人。

translations.literal: Thereupon, at ease in leisurely reading, he set his heart on the profound and mysterious, honored the extraordinary spirit of Dinghu, revered the lofty purity of Chao and You, sought counsel from the brilliant ministers, drew upon the talents of the host of lords, and thus yielded the great throne and transmitted the mandate to the sage.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon, at leisure he turned to profound learning, set his heart on the deepest truths, honored the extraordinary spirit of the Yellow Emperor at Dinghu, and revered the lofty purity of Chao Fu and Xu You. He sought counsel from brilliant ministers, drew upon the talents of the lords, and thus yielded the great throne and transmitted the mandate to the sage.

sentences.zh: 開古之高範，爰萃於一朝；

translations.literal: The lofty model opened since antiquity is here gathered in a single court;
translations.idiomatic: A lofty model opened since antiquity has here been gathered in a single age;

sentences.zh: 曠葉之希事，載見於今日。

translations.literal: a rare deed across vast ages is now seen in the present day.
translations.idiomatic: a deed rare across vast ages is now witnessed in our own day.

sentences.zh: 昔唐堯禪舜，前典大其成功；

translations.literal: Formerly Tang Yao abdicated to Shun; earlier classics greatly praised this achievement;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Tang Yao abdicated to Shun, and the earlier classics greatly praised that achievement;

sentences.zh: 太伯讓季，孔子稱其至德。

translations.literal: Taibo yielded to Ji; Confucius called this supreme virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Taibo yielded to Ji, and Confucius called this supreme virtue.

sentences.zh: 苟位以聖傳，臣子一也。

translations.literal: If the throne is transmitted through a sage, minister and subject are as one.
translations.idiomatic: If the throne passes through a sage, minister and subject are united in one purpose.

sentences.zh: 謹上至德頌一篇，其詞曰：

translations.literal: I respectfully submit one piece of praise to supreme virtue; its words say:
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully submit a hymn to supreme virtue; its words read:

sentences.zh: 茫茫太極，悠悠遐古。

translations.literal: Vast is the Supreme Ultimate; remote is distant antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Vast is the Supreme Ultimate; remote is distant antiquity.

sentences.zh: 三皇創制，五帝垂祜。

translations.literal: The Three Sovereigns created institutions; the Five Emperors bestowed blessings.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Sovereigns created institutions; the Five Emperors bestowed blessings.

sentences.zh: 仰察璿璣，俯鑒后土。

translations.literal: Looking up they observed the celestial pearl; looking down they mirrored the earthly sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up they observed the turning heavens; looking down they mirrored the earthly realm.

sentences.zh: 雍容端拱，惟德是與。

translations.literal: Dignified and composed, seated upright, they gave themselves only to virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Dignified and composed upon the throne, they gave themselves only to virtue.

sentences.zh: 夏殷世傳，周漢纂烈。

translations.literal: Xia and Yin passed the throne by succession; Zhou and Han inherited their glory.
translations.idiomatic: Xia and Yin passed the throne by succession; Zhou and Han inherited their glory.

sentences.zh: 道風雖邈，仍誕明哲。

translations.literal: Though the way and its influence are distant, wise and clear rulers still arise.
translations.idiomatic: Though the way and its influence lie far in the past, wise and enlightened rulers still arise.

sentences.zh: 爰暨三季，下凌上替。

translations.literal: Then came the three final ages, when the lower overbore the upper and order declined.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the three final ages, when the lower overbore the upper and order collapsed.

sentences.zh: 九服三分，禮樂四缺。

translations.literal: The Nine Domains were divided in three; rites and music were lacking on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Domains were divided in three; rites and music were broken on every side.

sentences.zh: 上靈降鑒，思皇反正。

translations.literal: The supreme spirit descended in judgment, thinking of the sovereign's return to the right path.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven descended in judgment, longing for the sovereign's return to the right path.

sentences.zh: 乃眷有魏，配天承命。

translations.literal: Then Wei was favored, matched with Heaven and received the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Then Wei was favored, matched with Heaven and received the mandate.

sentences.zh: 功冠前王，德侔往聖。

translations.literal: Its achievements surpass former kings; its virtue equals past sages.
translations.idiomatic: Its achievements surpass former kings; its virtue equals the sages of old.

sentences.zh: 移風革俗，天保載定。

translations.literal: It transformed customs and reformed practices; Heaven's protection was firmly established.
translations.idiomatic: It transformed customs and reformed practices; Heaven's protection was firmly established.

sentences.zh: 於穆太皇，克廣聖度。

translations.literal: Solemn is the Grand Emperor, able to extend the sage's measure.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn is the Grand Emperor, able to extend the sage's measure.

sentences.zh: 玄化外暢，惠鑒內悟。

translations.literal: The mysterious transformation flows outward; benevolent insight awakens within.
translations.idiomatic: The mysterious transformation flows outward; benevolent insight awakens within.

sentences.zh: 遺此崇高，挹彼沖素。

translations.literal: Leaving this exalted height, he draws upon that pure simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving this exalted height, he draws upon pure simplicity.

sentences.zh: 道映當今，慶流後祚。

translations.literal: The Way shines upon the present age; blessings flow to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Way shines upon the present age; blessings flow to later generations.

sentences.zh: 明明我皇，承乾紹煥。

translations.literal: Bright, bright is our emperor, inheriting Heaven and continuing its brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Bright, bright is our emperor, inheriting Heaven and continuing its brilliance.

sentences.zh: 比誦熙周，方文隆漢。

translations.literal: Comparable in renown to flourishing Zhou, comparable in culture to exalted Han.
translations.idiomatic: Comparable in renown to flourishing Zhou, comparable in culture to exalted Han.

sentences.zh: 重光麗天，晨暉疊旦。

translations.literal: Double brilliance adorns the sky; morning light layers upon dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Double brilliance adorns the sky; morning light layers upon dawn.

sentences.zh: 六府孔修，三辰貞觀。

translations.literal: The six treasuries are thoroughly ordered; the three luminaries stand in correct observation.
translations.idiomatic: The six treasuries are thoroughly ordered; the three luminaries stand in correct alignment.

sentences.zh: 功均乾造，雲覆雨潤。

translations.literal: His achievements equal Heaven's creation; like clouds covering and rain moistening.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements equal Heaven's creation; like clouds covering all and rain nourishing all.

sentences.zh: 養之以仁，敦之以信。

translations.literal: He nourishes them with benevolence and strengthens them with trust.
translations.idiomatic: He nourishes the people with benevolence and strengthens them with trust.

sentences.zh: 綏之斯和，動之斯震。

translations.literal: When he pacifies them, they harmonize; when he moves them, they tremble.
translations.idiomatic: When he pacifies them, they harmonize; when he moves them, they tremble.

sentences.zh: 自東徂西，無思不順。

translations.literal: From east to west, none who think do not submit.
translations.idiomatic: From east to west, none who think do not submit.

sentences.zh: 禎候並應，福祿來格。

translations.literal: Auspicious portents all respond; fortune and emolument arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious portents all respond; fortune and blessing arrive.

sentences.zh: 嘉穀秀町，素文表石。

translations.literal: Fine grain sprouts in the fields; white patterns appear on stone.
translations.idiomatic: Fine grain sprouts in the fields; white patterns appear on stone.

sentences.zh: 玄鳥呈皓，醴泉流液。

translations.literal: Dark birds display whiteness; sweet springs flow with nectar.
translations.idiomatic: Dark birds display whiteness; sweet springs flow with nectar.

sentences.zh: 黃龍蜿蜿，遊鱗奕奕。

translations.literal: Yellow dragons coil and wind; swimming scales gleam brightly.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow dragons coil and wind; swimming scales gleam brightly.

sentences.zh: 沖訓既布，率土咸寧。

translations.literal: Once the profound instruction is spread, all within the realm find peace.
translations.idiomatic: Once the profound instruction is spread, all within the realm find peace.

sentences.zh: 穆穆四門，灼灼典刑。

translations.literal: Solemn are the four gates; bright and clear are the exemplary punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn are the four gates; bright and clear are the exemplary punishments.

sentences.zh: 勝殘豈遠，期月有成。

translations.literal: Is overcoming cruelty still far off? In a full month there is achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Is overcoming cruelty still far off? In a full month there is achievement.

sentences.zh: 翹翹東岳，庶見翠旌。

translations.literal: Lofty, lofty is the Eastern Peak; may we see the green banner.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty, lofty is the Eastern Peak; may we see the green banner.

sentences.zh: 先民有言，千載一泰。

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: once in a thousand years comes a time of peace.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients had a saying: once in a thousand years comes a time of peace.

sentences.zh: 昔難其運，今易其會。

translations.literal: Formerly its fortune was hard to attain; now its moment comes easily.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly such fortune was hard to attain; now its moment comes easily.

sentences.zh: 沐浴淳澤，被服冠帶。

translations.literal: Bathed in pure bounty, clothed in cap and sash.
translations.idiomatic: Bathed in pure bounty, clothed in cap and sash.

sentences.zh: 飲和陶潤，載欣載賴。

translations.literal: Drinking harmony and soaking in gentle nurture, full of joy and reliance.
translations.idiomatic: Drinking harmony and soaking in gentle nurture, full of joy and gratitude.

sentences.zh: 文以寫意，功由頌宣。

translations.literal: Writing expresses intent; achievement is proclaimed through praise.
translations.idiomatic: Writing expresses intent; achievement is proclaimed through praise.

sentences.zh: 吉甫作歌，式昭永年。

translations.literal: Jifu composed the song to manifest eternal years.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu composed the song to manifest eternal years.

sentences.zh: 唐政緝熙，康哉垂篇。

translations.literal: Tang's governance was harmonious and bright; "How peaceful!" was handed down in a chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Tang's governance was harmonious and bright; "How peaceful!" was handed down in a chapter.

sentences.zh: 仰述徽烈，被之管絃。

translations.literal: Looking up I recount the illustrious achievements and set them to strings and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up I recount the illustrious achievements and set them to strings and pipes.

sentences.zh: 高允以閭文章富逸，舉以自代，遂為顯祖所知，數見引接，參論政治。

translations.literal: Gao Yun, because Lu's writings were rich and elegant, recommended him as his own successor; thus Lu came to be known to Emperor Xianzu, was repeatedly summoned and received, and participated in discussing government.
translations.idiomatic: Because Lu's writings were rich and elegant, Gao Yun recommended him as his own successor. Lu thus came to the attention of Emperor Xianwen, was repeatedly summoned to court, and took part in discussions of state policy.

sentences.zh: 命造鹿苑頌、北伐碑，顯祖善之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to compose "Praise of the Deer Park" and the "Northern Campaign Stele"; Emperor Xianzu approved them.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to compose "Praise of the Deer Park" and the "Northern Campaign Stele," and Emperor Xianwen was pleased with both.

sentences.zh: 承明初，為中書令，加給事中，委以機密。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chengming era, he served as Central Secretariat Director, given additional title Attendant Within the Gates, and entrusted with confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chengming era he was appointed Central Secretariat Director with the additional title Attendant Within the Gates and entrusted with confidential affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 文明太后甚重閭，詔令書檄碑銘贊頌皆其文也。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming greatly valued Lu; edicts, orders, letters, dispatches, stele inscriptions, praises, and eulogies were all his writing.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming held Lu in high esteem, and edicts, orders, letters, dispatches, stele inscriptions, praises, and eulogies were all written by him.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，出師討淮北，閭表曰：「伏見廟算有事淮海，雖成事不說，猶可思量。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Taihe era, the army marched out to attack north of the Huai. Lu submitted a memorial, saying: "I humbly see that the strategic planning concerns affairs in the Huai and sea region; though completed matters are not discussed, they may still be considered.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Taihe era, troops marched out to campaign against the region north of the Huai. Lu submitted a memorial that read, "I note that the court's strategic planning concerns the Huai and sea region. Though one does not speak of matters already settled, they may still be weighed."

sentences.zh: 臣以愚劣，本非武用，至於軍旅，尤所不學。

translations.literal: Your subject, being dull and inferior, is by nature no use for military affairs; as for armies and campaigns, it is what I least study.
translations.idiomatic: I am dull and unworthy by nature and no soldier; of all subjects, military affairs are what I have least studied.

sentences.zh: 直以無諱之朝，敢肆狂瞽，區區短見，竊有所疑。

translations.literal: Only because this is a court without taboos do I dare to indulge reckless blindness; with my petty short-sighted view, I privately have doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Only because this is a court where frank speech is permitted do I dare offer reckless counsel. From my limited perspective, I have private doubts.

sentences.zh: 臣聞兵者凶器，不得已而用之。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that weapons are inauspicious instruments, used only when there is no alternative.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that arms are inauspicious instruments, to be used only when there is no alternative.

sentences.zh: 今天下開泰，四方無虞，豈宜盛世，干戈妄動。

translations.literal: Now the realm is open and at peace, the four quarters free of alarm — how can a flourishing age wantonly stir weapons of war?
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is open and at peace, and the four quarters are free of alarm. How can a flourishing age wantonly stir weapons of war?

sentences.zh: 疑一也。

translations.literal: This is the first doubt.
translations.idiomatic: This is my first doubt.

sentences.zh: 淮北之城，凡有五處，難易相兼，皆須攻擊。

translations.literal: The cities north of the Huai number five in all; easy and difficult are mixed together, and all must be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: There are five cities north of the Huai in all, mixing easy and difficult targets, and each must be attacked.

sentences.zh: 然攻守難圖，力懸百倍，反覆思量，未見其利。

translations.literal: Yet attack and defense are hard to plan; the disparity in strength is a hundredfold. Turning it over again and again, I do not see the advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Yet attack and defense are hard to plan, and the disparity in strength is a hundredfold. After turning the matter over again and again, I see no advantage.

sentences.zh: 疑二也。

translations.literal: This is the second doubt.
translations.idiomatic: This is my second doubt.

sentences.zh: 縱使如心，於國無用，發兵遠入，費損轉多。

translations.literal: Even if all goes as wished, it is of no use to the state; sending troops far in, expense and loss only increase.
translations.idiomatic: Even if all goes as wished, it would be of no use to the state. Sending troops deep into enemy territory would only increase expense and loss.

sentences.zh: 若不置城，是謂空爭。

translations.literal: If cities are not established, this is called empty contention.
translations.idiomatic: If no garrison cities are established, the campaign would be empty contention.

sentences.zh: 疑三也。

translations.literal: This is the third doubt.
translations.idiomatic: This is my third doubt.

sentences.zh: 脫不如意，當延日月，屯眾聚費，于何不有。

translations.literal: If things do not go as wished, the campaign will drag on for months; massing troops and gathering expense — what would not be consumed?
translations.idiomatic: If things do not go as wished, the campaign will drag on for months, and the cost of massing troops and gathering supplies would be enormous.

sentences.zh: 疑四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth doubt.
translations.idiomatic: This is my fourth doubt.

sentences.zh: 伏願思此四疑，時速返旆。

translations.literal: I humbly wish that Your Majesty consider these four doubts and swiftly return the banners.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that Your Majesty consider these four doubts and withdraw the army at once.

sentences.zh: 」文明太后令曰：「六軍電發，有若摧朽，何慮四難也。」

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming issued an order: "The six armies strike like lightning, as if crushing rotten wood — why worry over four difficulties?"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming issued an order: "The six armies strike like lightning, as if crushing rotten wood. Why worry over four difficulties?"

sentences.zh: 遷尚書、中書監。

translations.literal: Transferred to Minister of the Secretariat and Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of the Secretariat and Director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 淮南王他奏求依舊斷祿，文明太后令召羣臣議之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Huainan, Ta, memorialized requesting that salaries be cut off as before. Empress Dowager Wenming ordered the ministers summoned to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Huainan, Ta, memorialized requesting that official salaries again be abolished. Empress Dowager Wenming ordered the ministers summoned to discuss the proposal.

sentences.zh: 閭表曰：

translations.literal: Lu submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Lu submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 天生烝民，樹之以君，明君不能獨理，必須臣以作輔。

translations.literal: Heaven gave birth to the multitude of people and set rulers over them. A wise ruler cannot govern alone and must have ministers to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven gave birth to the multitude of people and set rulers over them. A wise ruler cannot govern alone and must have ministers to assist him.

sentences.zh: 君使臣以禮，臣事君以忠。

translations.literal: The ruler employs ministers with ritual; ministers serve the ruler with loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler employs ministers with propriety; ministers serve the ruler with loyalty.

sentences.zh: 故車服有等差，爵命有分秩；

translations.literal: Therefore carriage and dress have gradations, and noble rank and appointment have separate orders;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore carriage and dress have gradations, and noble rank and appointment have their separate orders;

sentences.zh: 德高者則位尊，任廣者則祿重。

translations.literal: those of lofty virtue receive exalted position; those with broad responsibility receive heavy emolument.
translations.idiomatic: those of lofty virtue receive exalted position, and those with broad responsibility receive substantial emolument.

sentences.zh: 下者祿足以代耕，上者俸足以行義。

translations.literal: For the lower ranks, emolument suffices to substitute for farming; for the upper ranks, salary suffices to practice righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: For lower ranks, emolument suffices to replace farming; for upper ranks, salary suffices to practice righteousness.

sentences.zh: 庶民均其賦，以展奉上之心；

translations.literal: the common people evenly pay their levies to display the heart of serving above;
translations.idiomatic: the common people pay their levies evenly to show their devotion to those above;

sentences.zh: 君王聚其材，[2]以供事業之用。

translations.literal: the ruler gathers their resources to supply the needs of public affairs.
translations.idiomatic: and the ruler gathers their resources to supply the needs of public affairs.

sentences.zh: 君班其俸，垂惠則厚；

translations.literal: The ruler distributes salaries; bestowed favor is then generous;
translations.idiomatic: The ruler distributes salaries, and bestowed favor is generous;

sentences.zh: 臣受其祿，感恩則深。

translations.literal: ministers receive their emolument, and gratitude is then deep.
translations.idiomatic: ministers receive their emolument, and gratitude runs deep.

sentences.zh: 於是貪殘之心止，竭効之誠篤，兆庶無侵削之煩，百辟備禮容之美。

translations.literal: Thus the heart of greed and cruelty ceases, the sincerity of exhausting one's effort is earnest, the multitude have no trouble of encroachment and reduction, and the hundred ministers possess the beauty of ritual bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Thus greed and cruelty cease, sincere devotion flourishes, the people are spared the burden of exploitation, and the hundred ministers maintain the dignity of ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 斯則經世之明典，為治之至術。

translations.literal: This is the bright canon for ordering the age and the supreme technique of governance.
translations.idiomatic: This is the bright canon for ordering the age and the supreme technique of governance.

sentences.zh: 自堯舜以來，逮于三季，雖優劣不同，而斯道弗改。

translations.literal: From Yao and Shun down to the three final ages, though superior and inferior differed, this way was not altered.
translations.idiomatic: From Yao and Shun down to the three final ages, though standards differed in quality, this principle was never abandoned.

sentences.zh: 自中原崩否，天下幅裂，海內未一，民戶耗減，國用不充，俸祿遂廢。

translations.literal: Since the Central Plains collapsed and split apart, the realm was torn into pieces, the land within the seas was not unified, households dwindled, state revenue was insufficient, and salaries were therefore abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Central Plains collapsed and the realm was torn apart, the land was not unified, households dwindled, state revenue was insufficient, and official salaries were therefore abolished.

sentences.zh: 此則事出臨時之宜，良非長久之道。

translations.literal: This was a measure arising from temporary expediency and was truly not a long-term way.
translations.idiomatic: This was a measure born of temporary expediency and was truly not a long-term policy.

sentences.zh: 大魏應期紹祚，照臨萬方，九服既和，八表咸謐。

translations.literal: Great Wei received the mandate in its season and succeeded to the throne, shining over the myriad regions; the Nine Domains were already harmonized, the eight directions all tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Great Wei received the mandate in its season and succeeded to the throne, shining over the myriad regions. The Nine Domains were harmonized, and the eight directions were all at peace.

sentences.zh: 二聖欽明文思，道冠百代，動遵禮式，稽考舊章，準百王不易之勝法，述前聖利世之高軌，置立鄰黨，班宣俸祿，事設令行，於今已久，苛慝不生，上下無怨，姦巧革慮，闚覦絕心，利潤之厚，同於天地。

translations.literal: The two sages were reverent, bright in literary thought, their Way surpassing a hundred generations; in action they followed ritual forms, examined old statutes, measured against the unsurpassed laws of a hundred kings unchanged, set forth the lofty tracks of former sages that benefit the age, established neighborhood associations, distributed and proclaimed salaries — the matter was established and orders enforced, and from then until now it has been long. Harsh cruelty does not arise, above and below have no resentment, cunning and artifice change their intent, covetous longing ends in the heart, and the thickness of profit is equal to heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: The two sage rulers were reverent and brilliant in literary governance, their Way surpassing a hundred generations. In action they followed ritual forms, examined old statutes, measured themselves against the enduring laws of a hundred kings, and set forth the lofty paths of former sages that benefit the age. They established neighborhood associations and distributed official salaries. The system was established and enforced long ago. Harsh cruelty does not arise, above and below harbor no resentment, cunning and artifice change their intent, covetous longing dies in the heart, and the bounty of profit is as vast as heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 以斯觀之，如何可改？

translations.literal: Viewed in this light, how can it be altered?
translations.idiomatic: Viewed in this light, how can it be altered?

sentences.zh: 又洪波奔激，則隄防宜厚；

translations.literal: Moreover, when great waves rush and surge, dikes and defenses should be thick;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when great waves rush and surge, dikes and defenses should be thick;

sentences.zh: 姦悖充斥，則禁網須嚴。

translations.literal: when treachery and rebellion fill the land, prohibitions and nets must be strict.
translations.idiomatic: when treachery and rebellion fill the land, prohibitions and penalties must be strict.

sentences.zh: 且飢寒切身，慈母不保其子；

translations.literal: Moreover, when hunger and cold touch the body, even a loving mother cannot preserve her child;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when hunger and cold touch the body, even a loving mother cannot preserve her child;

sentences.zh: 家給人足，禮讓可得而生。

translations.literal: when every household has enough and every person is provided for, courtesy and yielding can arise.
translations.idiomatic: when every household has enough and every person is provided for, courtesy and yielding can arise.

sentences.zh: 但廉清之人，不必皆富；

translations.literal: Yet upright and pure persons are not necessarily all wealthy;
translations.idiomatic: Yet upright and honest officials are not necessarily all wealthy;

sentences.zh: 豐財之士，未必悉賢。

translations.literal: persons rich in wealth are not necessarily all worthy.
translations.idiomatic: and men rich in wealth are not necessarily all worthy.

sentences.zh: 今給其俸，則清者足以息其濫竊，貪者足以感而勸善；

translations.literal: Now, if salaries are granted, the upright will suffice to end their illicit taking, and the greedy will suffice to be moved and encouraged toward goodness;
translations.idiomatic: Now, if salaries are granted, the upright will no longer need to resort to illicit taking, and the greedy will be moved and encouraged toward goodness;

sentences.zh: 若不班祿，則貪者肆其姦情，清者不能自保。

translations.literal: if salaries are not distributed, the greedy will unleash their treacherous intent, and the upright cannot preserve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: if salaries are not distributed, the greedy will unleash their treacherous intent, and the upright cannot preserve themselves.

sentences.zh: 難易之驗，灼然可知，如何一朝便欲去俸？

translations.literal: The test of difficulty and ease is clearly knowable — how can one in a single morning wish to abolish salaries?
translations.idiomatic: The test of difficulty and ease is clearly knowable. How can one wish to abolish salaries in a single morning?

sentences.zh: 淮南之議，不亦謬乎？

translations.literal: Is not the proposal from Huainan absurd?
translations.idiomatic: Is not the proposal from Huainan absurd?

sentences.zh: 詔從閭議。

translations.literal: An edict followed Lu's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed Lu's proposal.

sentences.zh: 高祖又引見王公已下於皇信堂，高祖曰：「政雖多途，治歸一體，朕每蒙慈訓，猶自昧然。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen again summoned the princes and dukes and those below to the Huangxin Hall. Emperor Xiaowen said: "Though government has many paths, governance returns to one body. I constantly receive kind instruction, yet remain myself unclear.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen again summoned the princes, dukes, and officials below them to the Huangxin Hall. Emperor Xiaowen said, "Though government has many paths, governance returns to one body. I constantly receive kind instruction, yet remain myself unclear.

sentences.zh: 誠知忠佞有損益，而未識其異同，恒懼忠貞見毀，佞人便進。

translations.literal: I truly know that loyalty and flattery have benefit and harm, yet do not recognize their differences and similarities, and constantly fear that the loyal and upright will be slandered while flatterers will advance.
translations.idiomatic: I truly know that loyalty and flattery have benefit and harm, yet I do not recognize their differences and similarities, and I constantly fear that the loyal and upright will be slandered while flatterers advance.

sentences.zh: 寤寐思此，如有隱憂。

translations.literal: Waking and sleeping I think on this, as if with hidden sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Waking and sleeping I think on this, as if burdened by hidden sorrow.

sentences.zh: 國彥朝賢，休戚所共，宜辨斯真偽，以釋朕懷。

translations.literal: National worthies and court worthies share joy and sorrow with me; you should distinguish true from false to release what weighs on my heart.
translations.idiomatic: National worthies and court worthies share my joys and sorrows. You should distinguish true from false to ease what weighs on my heart."

sentences.zh: 」尚書游明根對曰：「忠佞之士，實亦難知，依古爵人，先試之以官，官定然後祿之，三載考績，然後忠佞可明。

translations.literal: Minister of the Secretariat You Minggen replied: "Loyal and flattering men are truly hard to know. Following the ancient method of evaluating men, first test them with office; once office is fixed, then grant emolument; after three years examine performance — then loyalty and flattery can be made clear.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Secretariat You Minggen replied, "Loyal and flattering men are truly hard to know. Following the ancient method of evaluating men, first test them with office; once office is fixed, then grant emolument. After three years examine performance, and then loyalty and flattery can be made clear.

sentences.zh: 」閭曰：「竊謂袁盎徹慎夫人席，是其忠；

translations.literal: Lu said: "I privately consider that Yuan Ang's removal of Lady Shen's seat was his loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: Lu said, "I would say that Yuan Ang's removal of Lady Shen's seat was an act of loyalty;

sentences.zh: 譖殺晁錯，是其佞。

translations.literal: slandering and causing the death of Chao Cuo was his flattery.
translations.idiomatic: and slandering Chao Cuo to his death was an act of flattery.

sentences.zh: 若以異人言之，望之為忠，石顯是佞。

translations.literal: If one speaks of different men, Wangzhi was loyal; Shi Xian was flattery.
translations.idiomatic: If one speaks of different men, Wangzhi was loyal and Shi Xian was a flatterer.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「自非聖人，忠佞之行，時或互有，但忠功顯即謂之忠，佞迹成斯謂之佞。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen said: "Except for sages, in the conduct of loyalty and flattery each may at times be mixed, but when loyal achievement is manifest it is called loyalty; when flattering traces are formed it is called flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said, "Except for sages, loyal and flattering conduct may at times be mixed in the same person, but when loyal achievement is manifest it is called loyalty, and when flattering traces are formed it is called flattery.

sentences.zh: 史官據成事而書，於今觀之，有別明矣。

translations.literal: Historians write according to completed deeds; viewed from today, the distinction is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Historians write according to completed deeds. Viewed from today, the distinction is clear.

sentences.zh: 朕所問者，未然之前；

translations.literal: What I ask about is before the deed is accomplished;
translations.idiomatic: What I ask about is before the deed is accomplished;

sentences.zh: 卿之所對，已然之後。

translations.literal: what you answer is after the deed is accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: what you answer is after the deed is accomplished.

sentences.zh: 」閭曰：「佞者，飾智以行事；

translations.literal: Lu said: "The flatterer adorns wisdom to conduct affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Lu said, "The flatterer adorns wisdom to conduct affairs;

sentences.zh: 忠者，發心以附道。

translations.literal: the loyal one sets forth the heart to attach to the Way.
translations.idiomatic: the loyal one sets forth the heart to attach to the Way.

sentences.zh: 譬如玉石，皦然可知。

translations.literal: It is like jade and stone — bright and clear, knowable at a glance.
translations.idiomatic: It is like jade and stone — bright and clear, knowable at a glance.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「玉石同體而異名，忠佞異名而同理。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen said: "Jade and stone share substance but differ in name; loyalty and flattery differ in name but share the same principle.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said, "Jade and stone share substance but differ in name; loyalty and flattery differ in name but share the same principle.

sentences.zh: 求之於同，則得其所以異；

translations.literal: Seek in what is the same, and you obtain what makes them different;
translations.idiomatic: Seek in what is the same, and you obtain what makes them different;

sentences.zh: 尋之於異，則失其所以同。

translations.literal: search in what is different, and you lose what makes them the same.
translations.idiomatic: search in what is different, and you lose what makes them the same.

sentences.zh: 出處同異之間，交換忠佞之境，豈是皦然易明哉？

translations.literal: Between the same and different in action and withdrawal, in the borderland where loyalty and flattery exchange — how can this be bright and clear, easy to discern?
translations.idiomatic: Between the same and different in action and withdrawal, in the borderland where loyalty and flattery exchange — how can this be bright and clear, easy to discern?

sentences.zh: 或有託佞以成忠，或有假忠以飾佞。

translations.literal: Some rely on flattery to accomplish loyalty; some borrow loyalty to adorn flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Some rely on flattery to accomplish loyalty; some borrow loyalty to adorn flattery.

sentences.zh: 如楚子綦後事顯忠，初非佞也。

translations.literal: Like Chu Ziqi — his later deeds show loyalty; at first he was not flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Take Chu Ziqi: his later deeds show loyalty, though at first he was not a flatterer.

sentences.zh: 」閭曰：「子綦諫楚，初雖隨述，終致忠言，此適欲幾諫，非為佞也。

translations.literal: Lu said: "Ziqi remonstrated with Chu; at first he followed along in narration, but in the end brought forth loyal words. This was simply intending indirect remonstrance — it was not flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu said, "Ziqi remonstrated with Chu. At first he followed along in narration, but in the end brought forth loyal words. This was simply indirect remonstrance — it was not flattery.

sentences.zh: 子綦若不設初權，後忠無由得顯。

translations.literal: If Ziqi had not set up the initial expedient, the later loyalty would have had no way to be displayed.
translations.idiomatic: If Ziqi had not set up the initial expedient, the later loyalty would have had no way to be displayed.

sentences.zh: 」高祖善閭對。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen approved of Lu's reply.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen approved of Lu's reply.

sentences.zh: 閭後上表曰：

translations.literal: Lu later submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Lu later submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞為國之道，其要有五：一曰文德，二曰武功，三曰法度，四曰防固，五曰刑賞。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the Way of governing a state has five essentials: first, civil virtue; second, martial achievement; third, laws and standards; fourth, defense and fortification; fifth, punishments and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the Way of governing a state has five essentials: first, civil virtue; second, martial achievement; third, laws and standards; fourth, defense and fortification; fifth, punishments and rewards.

sentences.zh: 故遠人不服，則修文德以來之；

translations.literal: Thus when distant peoples do not submit, cultivate civil virtue to draw them in;
translations.idiomatic: Thus when distant peoples do not submit, cultivate civil virtue to draw them in;

sentences.zh: 荒狡放命，則播武功以威之；

translations.literal: when wild and cunning peoples defy commands, spread martial achievement to awe them;
translations.idiomatic: when wild and cunning peoples defy commands, spread martial achievement to awe them;

sentences.zh: 民未知戰，則制法度以齊之；

translations.literal: when the people do not yet know warfare, establish laws and standards to align them;
translations.idiomatic: when the people do not yet know warfare, establish laws and standards to align them;

sentences.zh: 暴敵輕侵，則設防固以禦之；

translations.literal: when violent enemies lightly invade, set up defenses and fortifications to repel them;
translations.idiomatic: when violent enemies lightly invade, set up defenses and fortifications to repel them;

sentences.zh: 臨事制勝，則明刑賞以勸之。

translations.literal: when facing affairs and achieving victory, clarify punishments and rewards to encourage them.
translations.idiomatic: when facing affairs and achieving victory, clarify punishments and rewards to encourage them.

sentences.zh: 用能闢國寧方，征伐四克。

translations.literal: By this one can open the state and pacify the regions, and campaigns conquer on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: By this one can open the state and pacify the regions, and campaigns conquer on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 北狄悍愚，同於禽獸，所長者野戰，所短者攻城。

translations.literal: The northern Di are fierce and stupid, the same as birds and beasts; what they excel at is field battle, what they fall short in is storming cities.
translations.idiomatic: The northern Di are fierce and stupid, little better than birds and beasts. They excel at field battle and fall short at storming cities.

sentences.zh: 若以狄之所短，奪其所長，則雖眾不能成患，雖來不能內逼。

translations.literal: If one uses what the Di fall short in to seize what they excel at, then though numerous they cannot become a calamity, and though they come they cannot press inward.
translations.idiomatic: If one uses what the Di fall short in to neutralize what they excel at, then though numerous they cannot become a calamity, and though they come they cannot press inward.

sentences.zh: 又狄散居野澤，隨逐水草，戰則與家產並至，奔則與畜牧俱逃，不齎資糧而飲食足。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Di live scattered in wild marshes, following water and grass. When they fight, household goods come with them; when they flee, livestock flee together. They carry no provisions yet food and drink suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Di live scattered in wild marshes, following water and grass. When they fight, their household goods come with them; when they flee, their livestock flee together. They carry no provisions yet food and drink suffice.

sentences.zh: 是以古人伐北方，攘其侵掠而已。

translations.literal: Therefore the ancients in campaigning against the north merely repelled their raids and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the ancients in campaigning against the north merely repelled their raids and plunder.

sentences.zh: 歷代為邊患者，良以倏忽無常故也。

translations.literal: That successive ages suffered border troubles was truly because they were sudden and unpredictable.
translations.idiomatic: That successive ages suffered border troubles was truly because the Di were sudden and unpredictable.

sentences.zh: 六鎮勢分，倍眾不鬬，互相圍逼，難以制之。

translations.literal: The six garrisons' forces are divided; though double in number they do not fight; mutually surrounding and pressing, they are hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: The six garrisons' forces are divided. Though double in number they do not fight effectively, and mutually surrounding and pressing one another, they are hard to control.

sentences.zh: 昔周命南仲，城彼朔方；

translations.literal: Formerly Zhou commanded Nan Zhong to wall that northern region;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Zhou commanded Nan Zhong to wall the northern frontier;

sentences.zh: 趙靈、秦始，長城是築；

translations.literal: King Ling of Zhao and the First Emperor of Qin built the Long Wall;
translations.idiomatic: King Ling of Zhao and the First Emperor of Qin built the Long Wall;

sentences.zh: 漢之孝武，踵其前事。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Han followed their earlier deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han followed their earlier deeds.

sentences.zh: 此四代之君，皆帝王之雄傑，所以同此役者，非智術之不長，兵眾之不足，乃防狄之要事，其理宜然故也。

translations.literal: These rulers of four ages were all heroic emperors and kings. The reason they shared this task was not that their wisdom and methods were insufficient or their troops inadequate, but that defending against the Di was an essential matter — the principle rightly required it.
translations.idiomatic: These rulers of four ages were all heroic emperors and kings. The reason they shared this task was not that their wisdom and methods were insufficient or their troops inadequate, but that defending against the Di was an essential matter — the principle rightly required it.

sentences.zh: 易稱天險不可升，地險山川丘陵，王公設險以守其國，長城之謂歟？

translations.literal: The Changes says heaven's barriers cannot be ascended; earth's barriers are mountains, rivers, and hills. Kings and dukes set barriers to guard their states — is this not what the Long Wall means?
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says heaven's barriers cannot be ascended; earth's barriers are mountains, rivers, and hills. Kings and dukes set barriers to guard their states — is this not what the Long Wall means?

sentences.zh: 今宜依故於六鎮之北築長城，以禦北虜，雖有暫勞之勤，乃有永逸之益，如其一成，惠及百世。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to follow precedent and build the Long Wall north of the six garrisons to repel the northern invaders. Though there is temporary toil, there will be lasting ease; once it is completed, the benefit will extend for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Now it is fitting to follow precedent and build the Long Wall north of the six garrisons to repel the northern invaders. Though there is temporary toil, there will be lasting ease. Once it is completed, the benefit will extend for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 即於要害，往往開門，造小城於其側。

translations.literal: At strategic points, open gates here and there and build small cities at their sides.
translations.idiomatic: At strategic points, open gates here and there and build small cities beside them.

sentences.zh: 因地却敵，[3]多有弓弩。

translations.literal: Using the terrain to repel the enemy, there are many bows and crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Using the terrain to repel the enemy, station many bows and crossbows.

sentences.zh: 狄來有城可守，其兵可捍。

translations.literal: When the Di come, there are cities to hold and troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: When the Di come, there will be cities to hold and troops to resist.

sentences.zh: 既不攻城，野掠無獲，草盡則走，終必懲艾。

translations.literal: Since they cannot storm cities, their wild plunder gains nothing; when grass is exhausted they flee, and in the end they will surely be chastened.
translations.idiomatic: Since they cannot storm cities, their wild plunder gains nothing. When grass is exhausted they flee, and in the end they will surely be chastened.

sentences.zh: 宜發近州武勇四萬人及京師二萬人，合六萬人為武士，於苑內立征北大將軍府，選忠勇有志幹者以充其選。

translations.literal: It is fitting to mobilize forty thousand brave warriors from nearby provinces and twenty thousand from the capital, totaling sixty thousand as martial troops; establish the headquarters of the General Who Campaigns North within the park, and select men loyal, brave, and ambitious to fill the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to mobilize forty thousand brave warriors from nearby provinces and twenty thousand from the capital, totaling sixty thousand martial troops. Establish the headquarters of the General Who Campaigns North within the imperial park, and select men who are loyal, brave, and ambitious to fill the ranks.

sentences.zh: 下置官屬，分為三軍，二萬人專習弓射，二萬人專習戈盾，二萬人專習騎矟。

translations.literal: Below, establish official staff and divide into three armies: twenty thousand specialize in bow and shooting, twenty thousand specialize in halberd and shield, twenty thousand specialize in mounted lance.
translations.idiomatic: Below, establish official staff and divide them into three armies: twenty thousand specialize in bow and shooting, twenty thousand in halberd and shield, and twenty thousand in mounted lance.

sentences.zh: 修立戰場，十日一習，採諸葛亮八陣之法，為平地禦寇之方，使其解兵革之宜，識旌旗之節，器械精堅，必堪禦寇。

translations.literal: Establish training grounds, drill once every ten days, adopt Zhuge Liang's Eight Formations method as the method for repelling invaders on level ground, so that they understand the fitness of arms and armor, recognize the signals of banners and flags, and with refined and solid equipment will surely be able to repel invaders.
translations.idiomatic: Establish training grounds and drill once every ten days. Adopt Zhuge Liang's Eight Formations method as the technique for repelling invaders on level ground, so that the troops understand the proper use of arms and armor, recognize the signals of banners and flags, and with refined and solid equipment will surely be able to repel invaders.

sentences.zh: 使將有定兵，兵有常主，上下相信，晝夜如一。

translations.literal: Let generals have fixed troops, troops have regular commanders; above and below trust one another, day and night as one.
translations.idiomatic: Let generals have fixed troops and troops have regular commanders, so that above and below trust one another and act as one day and night.

sentences.zh: 七月發六部兵六萬人，各備戎作之具，敕臺北諸屯倉庫，隨近作米，俱送北鎮。

translations.literal: In the seventh month mobilize sixty thousand troops from the six divisions, each preparing military equipment; order the granaries and storehouses north of the capital to grind rice nearby and send it all to the northern garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month mobilize sixty thousand troops from the six divisions, each preparing military equipment. Order the granaries and storehouses north of the capital to grind rice nearby and send it all to the northern garrisons.

sentences.zh: 至八月，征北部率所領與六鎮之兵，直至磧南，揚威漠北。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the northern campaign headquarters would lead its forces together with the troops of the six garrisons straight to the south of the desert, displaying might north of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the northern campaign headquarters would lead its forces and the troops of the six garrisons straight to the south of the desert, displaying imperial might north of the desert.

sentences.zh: 狄若來拒，與之決戰，若其不來，然後散分其地，以築長城。

translations.literal: If the Di come to resist, fight a decisive battle with them; if they do not come, then divide and assign the land and build the Long Wall.
translations.idiomatic: If the Di come to resist, fight a decisive battle with them; if they do not come, then divide and assign the land and build the Long Wall.

sentences.zh: 計六鎮東西不過千里，若一夫一月之功，當三步之地，三百人三里，三千人三十里，三萬人三百里，則千里之地，強弱相兼，計十萬人一月必就，運糧一月不足為多。

translations.literal: Calculating that the six garrisons east to west span no more than a thousand li: if one man's labor in one month covers three paces of ground, three hundred men cover three li, three thousand men thirty li, and thirty thousand men three hundred li—then for a thousand li of land, strong and weak combined, a hundred thousand men would surely finish in one month, and transporting grain for one month would not be excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Calculating that the six garrisons east to west span no more than a thousand li: if one man's labor in one month covers three paces of ground, three hundred men cover three li, three thousand men thirty li, and thirty thousand men three hundred li—then for a thousand li of land, strong and weak combined, a hundred thousand men would surely finish in one month, and transporting grain for one month would not be excessive.

sentences.zh: 人懷永逸，勞而無怨。

translations.literal: The people would cherish lasting ease and toil without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The people would cherish lasting ease and toil without resentment.

sentences.zh: 計築長城，其利有五：罷遊防之苦，其利一也；

translations.literal: Calculating the building of the Long Wall, its benefits are five: ending the hardship of roaming defense—benefit one;
translations.idiomatic: Calculating the building of the Long Wall, its benefits are five: ending the hardship of roaming defense—benefit one;

sentences.zh: 北部放牧，無抄掠之患，其利二也；

translations.literal: northern pastures for herding without the trouble of raids—benefit two;
translations.idiomatic: northern pastures for herding without the trouble of raids—benefit two;

sentences.zh: 登城觀敵，以逸待勞，其利三也；

translations.literal: watching the enemy from the walls and awaiting them at ease—benefit three;
translations.idiomatic: watching the enemy from the walls and awaiting them at ease—benefit three;

sentences.zh: 省境防之虞，息無時之備，其利四也；

translations.literal: relieving border anxieties and ending constant readiness—benefit four;
translations.idiomatic: relieving border anxieties and ending constant readiness—benefit four;

sentences.zh: 歲常遊運，[4]永得不匱，其利五也。

translations.literal: annual transport by patrol would never be exhausted—benefit five.
translations.idiomatic: annual transport by patrol would never be exhausted—benefit five.

sentences.zh: 又任將之道，特須委信，遣之以禮，恕之以情，閫外之事，有利輒決，赦其小過，要其大功，足其兵力，資其給用，君臣相體，若身之使臂，然後忠勇可立，制勝可果。

translations.literal: Moreover, in employing generals, one must especially entrust them with confidence: send them forth with ritual, forgive them with kindness, let matters outside the gate be decided when advantageous, pardon small faults and demand great achievements, supply their troops fully, provide their needs, let ruler and minister be of one body like arm and hand—then loyalty and courage can be established and victory assured.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in employing generals, one must especially entrust them with confidence: send them forth with ritual propriety, forgive them with kindness, let matters outside the gate be decided when advantageous, pardon small faults and demand great achievements, supply their troops fully, provide their needs, let ruler and minister be of one body like arm and hand—then loyalty and courage can be established and victory assured.

sentences.zh: 是以忠臣盡其心，征將竭其力，雖三敗而踰榮，雖三背而彌寵。

translations.literal: Thus loyal ministers give their full hearts and campaigning generals exhaust their strength; though defeated three times they gain greater honor, though retreating three times they receive greater favor.
translations.idiomatic: Thus loyal ministers give their full hearts and campaigning generals exhaust their strength; though defeated three times they gain greater honor, though retreating three times they receive greater favor.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「覽表，具卿安邊之策。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Having read your memorial, I fully appreciate your strategy for securing the border.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Having read your memorial, I fully appreciate your strategy for securing the border.

sentences.zh: 比當與卿面論一二。」

translations.literal: I shall soon discuss the details with you face to face."
translations.idiomatic: I shall soon discuss the details with you face to face."

sentences.zh: 高祖又引見羣臣，議伐蠕蠕。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen again summoned the ministers and discussed campaigning against the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen again summoned the ministers and discussed campaigning against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「蠕蠕前後再擾朔邊，近有投化人云，敕勒渠帥興兵叛之，蠕蠕主身率徒眾，追至西漠。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Rouran have repeatedly disturbed the northern border. Recently a defector reported that the chieftain of the Tiele raised troops in rebellion, and the Rouran ruler personally led his followers in pursuit to the western desert.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The Rouran have repeatedly disturbed the northern border. Recently a defector reported that the chieftain of the Tiele raised troops in rebellion, and the Rouran ruler personally led his followers in pursuit to the western desert.

sentences.zh: 今為應乘弊致討，為應休兵息民？

translations.literal: Now should we seize this weakness to strike, or should we rest the troops and give the people peace?"
translations.idiomatic: Now should we seize this weakness to strike, or should we rest the troops and give the people peace?"

sentences.zh: 」左僕射穆亮對曰：「自古以來，有國有家莫不以戎事為首。

translations.literal: Left Deputy Director Mu Liang replied: "From antiquity, every state and every house has put military affairs first.
translations.idiomatic: Left Deputy Director Mu Liang replied: "From antiquity, every state and every house has put military affairs first.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕子孫，襲其凶業，頻為寇擾，為惡不悛，自相違叛。

translations.literal: The descendants of the Rouran inherit their vicious enterprise, repeatedly raiding as bandits, doing evil without repentance, and now turn against one another in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The descendants of the Rouran inherit their vicious enterprise, repeatedly raiding as bandits, doing evil without repentance, and now turn against one another in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 如臣愚見，宜興軍討之，雖不頓除巢穴，且以挫其醜勢。

translations.literal: In my humble view, it is fitting to raise an army to punish them; though their nest may not be destroyed at once, at least their ugly momentum will be broken.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, it is fitting to raise an army to punish them; though their nest may not be destroyed at once, at least their ugly momentum will be broken.

sentences.zh: 」閭曰：「昔漢時天下一統，故得窮追北狄，今南有吳寇，不宜懸軍深入。

translations.literal: Lu said: "In Han times the realm was unified, and therefore they could pursue the northern Di to the end. Now there are Wu bandits in the south—it is not fitting to suspend the army and advance deep.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu said: "In Han times the realm was unified, and therefore they could pursue the northern Di to the end. Now there are Wu bandits in the south—it is not fitting to suspend the army and advance deep.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「先朝屢興征伐者，以有未賓之虜。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen said: "Former emperors repeatedly launched campaigns because there were unsubmissive barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said: "Former emperors repeatedly launched campaigns because there were unsubmissive barbarians.

sentences.zh: 朕承太平之基，何為搖動兵革？

translations.literal: I inherit a foundation of peace—why should I stir up arms?
translations.idiomatic: I inherit a foundation of peace—why should I stir up arms?

sentences.zh: 夫兵者凶器，聖王不得已而用之。

translations.literal: Weapons are instruments of ill omen; sage kings use them only when they have no choice.
translations.idiomatic: Weapons are instruments of ill omen; sage kings use them only when they have no choice.

sentences.zh: 便可停也。

translations.literal: Let the campaign be halted."
translations.idiomatic: Let the campaign be halted."

sentences.zh: 」高祖又曰：「今欲遣蠕蠕使還，應有書問以不？

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen also said: "Now we wish to send the Rouran envoy back—should there be a letter of inquiry or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen also said: "Now we wish to send the Rouran envoy back—should there be a letter of inquiry or not?"

sentences.zh: 」羣臣以為宜有，乃詔閭為書。

translations.literal: The ministers thought there should be one, and so Lu was ordered to compose the letter.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers thought there should be one, and so Gao Lu was ordered to compose the letter.

sentences.zh: 於時蠕蠕國有喪，而書不敍凶事。

translations.literal: At that time the Rouran state was in mourning, but the letter did not mention the bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Rouran state was in mourning, but the letter did not mention the bereavement.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿為中書監，職典文詞，所造旨書，不論彼之凶事。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen said: "You serve as Director of the Secretariat, with charge over literary composition. The imperial letter you drafted makes no mention of their bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said: "You serve as Director of the Secretariat, with charge over literary composition. The imperial letter you drafted makes no mention of their bereavement.

sentences.zh: 若知而不作，罪在灼然，若情思不至，應謝所任。

translations.literal: If you knew and did not write it, the guilt is clear; if your intent did not reach that far, you should resign your office."
translations.idiomatic: If you knew and did not write it, the guilt is clear; if your intent did not reach that far, you should resign your office."

sentences.zh: 」閭對曰：「昔蠕蠕主敦崇和親，其子不遵父志，屢犯邊境，如臣愚見，謂不宜弔。

translations.literal: Lu replied: "Formerly the Rouran ruler honored harmony and kinship, but his son did not follow his father's will and repeatedly violated the border. In my humble view, it is not fitting to send condolences."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu replied: "Formerly the Rouran ruler honored harmony and kinship, but his son did not follow his father's will and repeatedly violated the border. In my humble view, it is not fitting to send condolences."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「敬其父則子悅，敬其君則臣悅。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen said: "Honor his father and the son will be pleased; honor his ruler and the minister will be pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said: "Honor his father and the son will be pleased; honor his ruler and the minister will be pleased.

sentences.zh: 卿云不合弔慰，是何言歟！

translations.literal: You say it is not fitting to send condolences—what kind of talk is this!"
translations.idiomatic: You say it is not fitting to send condolences—what kind of talk is this!"

sentences.zh: 」閭遂引愆，免冠謝罪。

translations.literal: Lu thereupon acknowledged his fault, removed his cap, and begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu thereupon acknowledged his fault, removed his cap, and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂閭曰：「蠕蠕使牟提小心恭慎，甚有使人之禮，同行疾其敦厚，每至陵辱，恐其還北，必被謗誣。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen said to Lu: "The Rouran envoy Mouti is careful and reverent and has the deportment of a proper envoy. His companions on the journey resent his earnest integrity and constantly insult him. I fear that when he returns north he will surely be slandered.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said to Gao Lu: "The Rouran envoy Mouti is careful and reverent and has the deportment of a proper envoy. His companions on the journey resent his earnest integrity and constantly insult him. I fear that when he returns north he will surely be slandered.

sentences.zh: 昔劉準使殷靈誕每禁下人不為非禮之事，及其還國，果被譖愬，以致極刑。

translations.literal: Formerly when Liu Zhun sent Yin Lingdan, he constantly forbade his subordinates from improper conduct; when Yin returned home, he was indeed slandered and suffered the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when Liu Zhun sent Yin Lingdan, he constantly forbade his subordinates from improper conduct; when Yin returned home, he was indeed slandered and suffered the extreme penalty.

sentences.zh: 今為旨書，可明牟提忠於其國，使蠕蠕主知之。」

translations.literal: Now compose an imperial letter making clear that Mouti is loyal to his state, so that the Rouran ruler may know it."
translations.idiomatic: Now compose an imperial letter making clear that Mouti is loyal to his state, so that the Rouran ruler may know it."

sentences.zh: 是年冬至，高祖、文明太后大饗羣官，高祖親舞於太后前，羣臣皆舞。

translations.literal: That year at the winter solstice, Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming held a great feast for the officials. Emperor Xiaowen danced before the empress dowager, and all the ministers danced as well.
translations.idiomatic: That year at the winter solstice, Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming held a great feast for the officials. Emperor Xiaowen danced before the empress dowager, and all the ministers danced as well.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃歌，仍率羣臣再拜上壽。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen then sang and led the ministers in bowing twice to offer longevity wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen then sang and led the ministers in bowing twice to offer longevity wishes.

sentences.zh: 閭進曰：「臣聞：大夫行孝，行合一家；

translations.literal: Lu stepped forward and said: "I have heard: when a grand officer practices filial piety, his conduct harmonizes one household;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu stepped forward and said: "I have heard: when a grand officer practices filial piety, his conduct harmonizes one household;

sentences.zh: 諸侯行孝，聲著一國；

translations.literal: when a feudal lord practices filial piety, his fame resounds through one state;
translations.idiomatic: when a feudal lord practices filial piety, his fame resounds through one state;

sentences.zh: 天子行孝，德被四海。

translations.literal: when the Son of Heaven practices filial piety, his virtue covers the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: when the Son of Heaven practices filial piety, his virtue covers the four seas.

sentences.zh: 今陛下聖性自天，敦行孝道，稱觴上壽，靈應無差，臣等不勝慶踊，謹上千萬歲壽。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's sacred nature comes from Heaven, and you earnestly practice filial piety. Raising the cup to offer longevity, spiritual responses are without error. Your servants cannot contain our joy and leap for joy, and respectfully offer wishes for ten thousand years of life."
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty's sacred nature comes from Heaven, and you earnestly practice filial piety. Raising the cup to offer longevity, spiritual responses are without error. Your servants cannot contain our joy and leap for joy, and respectfully offer wishes for ten thousand years of life."

sentences.zh: 」高祖大悅，賜羣臣帛，人三十匹。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen was greatly pleased and bestowed silk on the ministers, thirty bolts per man.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen was greatly pleased and bestowed silk on the ministers, thirty bolts per man.

sentences.zh: 又議政於皇信堂，高祖曰：「百揆多途，萬機事猥，未周之闕，卿等宜有所陳。

translations.literal: They again discussed government in the Huangxin Hall. Emperor Xiaowen said: "The hundred offices have many paths, and the myriad affairs are numerous; wherever there are gaps, you should speak of them.
translations.idiomatic: They again discussed government in the Huangxin Hall. Emperor Xiaowen said: "The hundred offices have many paths, and the myriad affairs are numerous; wherever there are gaps, you should speak of them.

sentences.zh: 」閭對曰：「臣伏思太皇太后十八條之令，及仰尋聖朝所行，事周於百揆，理兼於庶務。

translations.literal: Lu replied: "Your servant has reflected on the eighteen commands of the Grand Empress Dowager and, looking up, traced what the sacred court has carried out—affairs that encompass the hundred offices and principles that cover the multitude of tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu replied: "Your servant has reflected on the eighteen commands of the Grand Empress Dowager and, looking up, traced what the sacred court has carried out—affairs that encompass the hundred offices and principles that cover the multitude of tasks.

sentences.zh: 孔子至聖，三年有成；

translations.literal: Confucius, the utmost sage, achieved results in three years;
translations.idiomatic: Confucius, the utmost sage, achieved results in three years;

sentences.zh: 子產治鄭，歷載乃就。

translations.literal: Zichan governed Zheng, and only after years did he succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Zichan governed Zheng, and only after years did he succeed.

sentences.zh: 今聖化方宣，風政驟改，行之積久，自然致治，理之必明，不患事闕。

translations.literal: Now the sacred transformation is just being proclaimed and customs and policies are changing swiftly; if carried out over time, good governance will naturally be achieved. The principle is sure to become clear—there is no worry over missing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Now the sacred transformation is just being proclaimed and customs and policies are changing swiftly; if carried out over time, good governance will naturally be achieved. The principle is sure to become clear—there is no worry over missing affairs.

sentences.zh: 又為政之道，終始若一，民可使由之，不可使知之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the way of governance begins and ends as one; the people may be made to follow it, but cannot be made to understand it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the way of governance begins and ends as one; the people may be made to follow it, but cannot be made to understand it.

sentences.zh: 政令既宣，若有不合於民者，因民之心而改之。

translations.literal: Once policies are promulgated, if any do not accord with the people's hearts, change them according to the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Once policies are promulgated, if any do not accord with the people's hearts, change them according to the people's hearts.
