sentences.zh: 願終成其事，使至教必行。

translations.literal: I wish that you will carry matters through to completion, so that the utmost teaching will surely be put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: I wish that you will carry matters through to completion, so that the utmost teaching will surely be put into practice.

sentences.zh: 臣反覆三思，理畢於此，不知其他。

translations.literal: Your servant has reflected three times and the principle ends here—I know nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has reflected three times and the principle ends here—I know nothing else.

sentences.zh: 但使今之法度，必理、必明、必行、必久，勝殘去殺，可不遠而致。

translations.literal: But if the laws and institutions of today are sure to be ordered, clear, enforced, and enduring, then overcoming cruelty and abolishing killing can be achieved before long.
translations.idiomatic: But if the laws and institutions of today are sure to be ordered, clear, enforced, and enduring, then overcoming cruelty and abolishing killing can be achieved before long.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「刑法者，王道之所用。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen said: "Penal law is what the way of kings employs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said: "Penal law is what the way of kings employs.

sentences.zh: 何者為法？

translations.literal: What is law?
translations.idiomatic: What is law?

sentences.zh: 何者為刑？

translations.literal: What is punishment?
translations.idiomatic: What is punishment?

sentences.zh: 施行之日，何先何後？

translations.literal: On the day of implementation, what comes first and what comes after?"
translations.idiomatic: On the day of implementation, what comes first and what comes after?"

sentences.zh: 」閭對曰：「臣聞創制立會，[5]軌物齊眾，謂之法；

translations.literal: Lu replied: "I have heard that creating institutions and establishing standards, [5] aligning things and gathering the multitude—this is called law;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu replied: "I have heard that creating institutions and establishing standards, [5] aligning things and gathering the multitude—this is called law;

sentences.zh: 犯違制約，致之於憲，謂之刑。

translations.literal: violating and transgressing the established rules and bringing one to punishment—this is called penal sanction.
translations.idiomatic: violating and transgressing the established rules and bringing one to punishment—this is called penal sanction.

sentences.zh: 然則法必先施，刑必後著。

translations.literal: Thus law must first be applied, and punishment must afterward be made manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Thus law must first be applied, and punishment must afterward be made manifest.

sentences.zh: 自鞭杖已上至於死罪，皆謂之刑。

translations.literal: From beating with the rod up to the death penalty—all are called punishment.
translations.idiomatic: From beating with the rod up to the death penalty—all are called punishment.

sentences.zh: 刑者，成也，成而不可改。

translations.literal: Punishment means completion—once completed it cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment means completion—once completed it cannot be changed.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「論語稱：『冉子退朝，孔子問曰：何晏也？

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen said: "The Analects says: 'When Ran Qiu withdrew from court, Confucius asked: Why so late?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said: "The Analects says: 'When Ran Qiu withdrew from court, Confucius asked: Why so late?

sentences.zh: 對曰：有政。

translations.literal: He replied: There was government business.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: There was government business.

sentences.zh: 子曰：其事也。

translations.literal: The Master said: That was an affair.
translations.idiomatic: The Master said: That was an affair.

sentences.zh: 如有政，雖不吾以，吾其與聞之。

translations.literal: If there were government business, though he did not employ me, I would surely have heard of it.'
translations.idiomatic: If there were government business, though he did not employ me, I would surely have heard of it.'

sentences.zh: 』何者是政？

translations.literal: What is government?
translations.idiomatic: What is government?

sentences.zh: 何者為事？

translations.literal: What is an affair?"
translations.idiomatic: What is an affair?"

sentences.zh: 」閭對曰：「臣聞：政者，君上之所施行，合於法度，經國治民之屬，皆謂之政；

translations.literal: Lu replied: "I have heard: government is what the ruler above carries out, in accord with laws and institutions, belonging to the category of ordering the state and governing the people;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu replied: "I have heard: government is what the ruler above carries out, in accord with laws and institutions, belonging to the category of ordering the state and governing the people;

sentences.zh: 臣下奉教承旨，作而行之，謂之事。

translations.literal: ministers below receive edicts and carry out orders, acting and executing them—this is called an affair.
translations.idiomatic: ministers below receive edicts and carry out orders, acting and executing them—this is called an affair.

sentences.zh: 然則天下大同，風軌齊一，則政出於天子；

translations.literal: When the realm is greatly unified and customs and standards are aligned, then government issues from the Son of Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: When the realm is greatly unified and customs and standards are aligned, then government issues from the Son of Heaven;

sentences.zh: 王道衰，則政出於諸侯；

translations.literal: when the way of kings declines, then government issues from the feudal lords;
translations.idiomatic: when the way of kings declines, then government issues from the feudal lords;

sentences.zh: 君道缺，則政出於大夫。

translations.literal: when the way of the ruler is deficient, then government issues from grand officers.
translations.idiomatic: when the way of the ruler is deficient, then government issues from grand officers.

sentences.zh: 故詩序曰：『王道衰，政教失，則國異政，家殊俗。

translations.literal: Therefore the Preface to the Odes says: 'When the way of kings declines and teaching and transformation are lost, then states have different governments and families have different customs.'
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Preface to the Odes says: 'When the way of kings declines and teaching and transformation are lost, then states have different governments and families have different customs.'

sentences.zh: 』政者，上之所行；

translations.literal: Government is what those above carry out;
translations.idiomatic: Government is what those above carry out;

sentences.zh: 事者，下之所奉。

translations.literal: affairs are what those below undertake.
translations.idiomatic: affairs are what those below undertake.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「若君命為政，子夏為莒父宰，問政，此應奉命而已，何得稱政？

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen said: "If the ruler's command is called government, when Zixia became magistrate of Jufu and asked about government—should this not mean merely receiving orders? How can it be called government?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said: "If the ruler's command is called government, when Zixia became magistrate of Jufu and asked about government—should this not mean merely receiving orders? How can it be called government?"

sentences.zh: 」尚書游明根曰：「子夏宰民，故得稱政。

translations.literal: Minister of the Secretariat You Minggen said: "Zixia governed the people, and therefore could be said to govern.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Secretariat You Minggen said: "Zixia governed the people, and therefore could be said to govern.

sentences.zh: 」帝善之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved of this.

sentences.zh: 十四年秋，閭上表曰：

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourteenth year, Lu submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourteenth year, Gao Lu submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 奉癸未詔書，以春夏少雨，憂飢饉之方臻，愍黎元之傷瘁。

translations.literal: In accordance with the edict of the guwei day, because spring and summer had little rain, I worried that famine would soon arrive and pitied the common people in their suffering.
translations.idiomatic: In accordance with the edict of the guwei day, because spring and summer had little rain, I worried that famine would soon arrive and pitied the common people in their suffering.

sentences.zh: 同禹湯罪己之誠，齊堯舜引咎之德，虞災致懼，詢及卿士，令各上書，極陳損益。

translations.literal: Together with Yu and Tang's sincerity in blaming themselves, and equal to Yao and Shun's virtue in taking blame upon themselves, you responded to calamity with fear and consulted the ministers, ordering each to submit a memorial fully setting forth benefits and harms.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Yu and Tang's sincerity in blaming themselves, and equal to Yao and Shun's virtue in taking blame upon themselves, you responded to calamity with fear and consulted the ministers, ordering each to submit a memorial fully setting forth benefits and harms.

sentences.zh: 深恩被於蒼生，厚惠流于后土。

translations.literal: Deep grace covers the black-haired people; thick bounty flows to the land below.
translations.idiomatic: Deep grace covers the black-haired people; thick bounty flows to the land below.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下天啟聖姿，利見纂極，欽若昊天，光格宇宙。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty was Heaven-endowed with a sacred disposition, auspiciously ascending the throne, reverently following vast Heaven, and illuminating the universe.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty was Heaven-endowed with a sacred disposition, auspiciously ascending the throne, reverently following vast Heaven, and illuminating the universe.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后以叡哲贊世，稽合三才，高明柔克，道被無外。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager, with sagely wisdom aiding the age, harmonized the three powers; lofty, bright, gentle, and yielding, her way extended without limit.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager, with sagely wisdom aiding the age, harmonized the three powers; lofty, bright, gentle, and yielding, her way extended without limit.

sentences.zh: 七政昭宣於上，九功咸序於下。

translations.literal: The seven regulators were proclaimed above and the nine achievements were all ordered below.
translations.idiomatic: The seven regulators were proclaimed above and the nine achievements were all ordered below.

sentences.zh: 君人之量逾高，謙光之旨彌篤。

translations.literal: The measure of one who rules men grows ever higher; the intent of humble grace grows ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: The measure of one who rules men grows ever higher; the intent of humble grace grows ever deeper.

sentences.zh: 修復祭儀，宗廟所以致敬；

translations.literal: Restoring sacrificial rites—thus the ancestral temple receives due reverence;
translations.idiomatic: Restoring sacrificial rites—thus the ancestral temple receives due reverence;

sentences.zh: 飾正器服，禮樂所以宣和。

translations.literal: correcting vessels and dress—thus rites and music spread harmony.
translations.idiomatic: correcting vessels and dress—thus rites and music spread harmony.

sentences.zh: 增儒官以重文德，簡勇士以昭武功。

translations.literal: Increasing Confucian offices to honor civil virtue; selecting brave warriors to display martial achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Increasing Confucian offices to honor civil virtue; selecting brave warriors to display martial achievement.

sentences.zh: 慮獄訟之未息，定刑書以理之；

translations.literal: Concerned that litigation had not ceased, you fixed the penal code to order it;
translations.idiomatic: Concerned that litigation had not ceased, you fixed the penal code to order it;

sentences.zh: 懼蒸民之姦宄，置鄰黨以穆之；

translations.literal: fearing wickedness among the people, you established neighborhood groups to harmonize them;
translations.idiomatic: fearing wickedness among the people, you established neighborhood groups to harmonize them;

sentences.zh: 究庶官之勤劇，班俸祿以優之；

translations.literal: examining the toil of the multitude of officials, you distributed salaries to honor them;
translations.idiomatic: examining the toil of the multitude of officials, you distributed salaries to honor them;

sentences.zh: 知勞逸之難均，分民土以齊之。

translations.literal: knowing the difficulty of balancing labor and rest, you divided land among the people to equalize it.
translations.idiomatic: knowing the difficulty of balancing labor and rest, you divided land among the people to equalize it.

sentences.zh: 甄忠明孝，矜貧恤獨，開納讜言，抑絕讒佞，明訓以體，率土移風。

translations.literal: You distinguished the loyal and enlightened in filial piety, pitied the poor and comforted the solitary, opened the way for candid speech, suppressed slander and flattery, clarified instruction through substance, and moved customs throughout the land.
translations.idiomatic: You distinguished the loyal and enlightened in filial piety, pitied the poor and comforted the solitary, opened the way for candid speech, suppressed slander and flattery, clarified instruction through substance, and moved customs throughout the land.

sentences.zh: 雖未勝殘去殺，成無為之化，足以仰答三靈者矣。

translations.literal: Though you have not yet overcome cruelty and abolished killing, achieving the transformation of non-action, it is enough to answer the three spirits on high.
translations.idiomatic: Though you have not yet overcome cruelty and abolished killing, achieving the transformation of non-action, it is enough to answer the three spirits on high.

sentences.zh: 臣聞皇天無私，降鑒在下，休咎之徵，咸由人召。

translations.literal: I have heard that august Heaven is without partiality and sends down scrutiny below; omens of blessing and calamity are all summoned by men.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that august Heaven is without partiality and sends down scrutiny below; omens of blessing and calamity are all summoned by men.

sentences.zh: 故帝道昌則九疇敍，君德衰而彝倫斁。

translations.literal: Therefore when the way of emperors flourishes, the nine categories are ordered; when the virtue of rulers declines, normal human relations are destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when the way of emperors flourishes, the nine categories are ordered; when the virtue of rulers declines, normal human relations are destroyed.

sentences.zh: 休瑞並應，享以五福，則康于其邦；

translations.literal: When blessings and auspicious signs respond together and one enjoys the five blessings, then there is peace in the state;
translations.idiomatic: When blessings and auspicious signs respond together and one enjoys the five blessings, then there is peace in the state;

sentences.zh: 咎徵屢臻，罰以六極，則害于其國。

translations.literal: when calamitous signs repeatedly arrive and one is punished with the six extremes, then there is harm to the state.
translations.idiomatic: when calamitous signs repeatedly arrive and one is punished with the six extremes, then there is harm to the state.

sentences.zh: 斯乃洪範之實徵，神祇之明驗。

translations.literal: This is the solid proof of the Great Plan and the clear verification of the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: This is the solid proof of the Great Plan and the clear verification of the spirits.

sentences.zh: 及其厄運所纏，世鍾陽九，數乖於天理，事違於人謀，時則有之矣。

translations.literal: When ill fortune binds the age and the world meets the yang ninth period, numbers depart from Heaven's principle and affairs violate human planning—then such times do occur.
translations.idiomatic: When ill fortune binds the age and the world meets the yang ninth period, numbers depart from Heaven's principle and affairs violate human planning—then such times do occur.

sentences.zh: 故堯湯逢歷年之災，周漢遭水旱之患，然立功修行，終能弭息。

translations.literal: Therefore Yao and Tang encountered disasters lasting years, and Zhou and Han suffered from flood and drought; yet by establishing merit and practicing the Way, they were finally able to quell them.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Yao and Tang encountered disasters lasting years, and Zhou and Han suffered from flood and drought; yet by establishing merit and practicing the Way, they were finally able to quell them.

sentences.zh: 今考治則有如此之風，計運未有如彼之害，而陛下殷勤引過，事邁前王。

translations.literal: Now when I examine governance, there is such excellence as this, and when I calculate fortune, there is not such harm as that—yet Your Majesty earnestly takes blame upon yourself, surpassing former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Now when I examine governance, there is such excellence as this, and when I calculate fortune, there is not such harm as that—yet Your Majesty earnestly takes blame upon yourself, surpassing former kings.

sentences.zh: 徙星澍雨之徵，[6]指辰可必；

translations.literal: The signs of moving stars and abundant rain, [6] can be awaited at the appointed time;
translations.idiomatic: The signs of moving stars and abundant rain, [6] can be awaited at the appointed time;

sentences.zh: 消災滅禍之符，灼然自見。

translations.literal: the tokens of dispelling disaster and extinguishing calamity are clearly visible.
translations.idiomatic: the tokens of dispelling disaster and extinguishing calamity are clearly visible.

sentences.zh: 雖王畿之內，頗為少雨，關外諸方，禾稼仍茂，苟動之以禮，綏之以和，一歲不收，未為大損。

translations.literal: Though within the royal domain rain has been somewhat scarce, in regions beyond the passes the grain crops are still abundant. If moved by ritual and pacified with harmony, one poor harvest is not a great loss.
translations.idiomatic: Though within the royal domain rain has been somewhat scarce, in regions beyond the passes the grain crops are still abundant. If moved by ritual and pacified with harmony, one poor harvest is not a great loss.

sentences.zh: 但豫備不虞，古之善政，安不忘危，有國常典。

translations.literal: But preparing against the unexpected is the good governance of antiquity; in security do not forget danger—this is the constant rule of a state.
translations.idiomatic: But preparing against the unexpected is the good governance of antiquity; in security do not forget danger—this is the constant rule of a state.

sentences.zh: 竊以北鎮新徙，家業未就，思親戀本，人有愁心，一朝有事，難以禦敵。

translations.literal: I privately consider that the northern garrisons were recently relocated, households and enterprises are not yet established, and the people long for kin and their native places with sorrow in their hearts. If trouble arises suddenly, it will be hard to repel the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: I privately consider that the northern garrisons were recently relocated, households and enterprises are not yet established, and the people long for kin and their native places with sorrow in their hearts. If trouble arises suddenly, it will be hard to repel the enemy.

sentences.zh: 可寬其往來，頗使欣慰，開雲中馬城之食以賑恤之，[7]足以感德，致力邊境矣。

translations.literal: Broaden their coming and going and greatly give them comfort. Open the grain stores of Yunzhong and Macheng for relief, [7] enough to move them with virtue and make them devote themselves to the border.
translations.idiomatic: Broaden their coming and going and greatly give them comfort. Open the grain stores of Yunzhong and Macheng for relief, [7] enough to move them with virtue and make them devote themselves to the border.

sentences.zh: 明察畿甸之民，飢甚者，出靈丘下館之粟以救其乏，可以安慰孤貧，樂業保土。

translations.literal: Clearly examine the people of the capital region; where hunger is severe, release grain from Lingqiu and the lower lodges to relieve their want, enough to comfort the orphaned and poor and keep them content in their lands.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly examine the people of the capital region; where hunger is severe, release grain from Lingqiu and the lower lodges to relieve their want, enough to comfort the orphaned and poor and keep them content in their lands.

sentences.zh: 使幽、定、安、并四州之租，隨運以溢其處；

translations.literal: Have the tax grain of the four provinces of You, Ding, An, and Bing transported as it is collected to where it overflows;
translations.idiomatic: Have the tax grain of the four provinces of You, Ding, An, and Bing transported as it is collected to where it overflows;

sentences.zh: [8]開關㢮禁，薄賦賤糴，以消其費；

translations.literal: [8] open the passes and relax prohibitions, reduce levies and sell grain cheaply, to lessen expense;
translations.idiomatic: [8] open the passes and relax prohibitions, reduce levies and sell grain cheaply, to lessen expense;

sentences.zh: 清道路，恣其東西，隨豐遂食，貧富相贍。

translations.literal: clear the roads and allow free movement east and west; follow abundance and eat accordingly, rich and poor supporting one another.
translations.idiomatic: clear the roads and allow free movement east and west; follow abundance and eat accordingly, rich and poor supporting one another.

sentences.zh: 可以免度凶年，不為患苦。

translations.literal: Thus one can pass through a famine year without becoming a source of suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one can pass through a famine year without becoming a source of suffering.

sentences.zh: 又聞常士困則濫竊生，匹婦餒則慈心薄。

translations.literal: I also hear that when ordinary men are distressed, unlawful taking arises; when a single woman is hungry, maternal tenderness grows thin.
translations.idiomatic: I also hear that when ordinary men are distressed, unlawful taking arises; when a single woman is hungry, maternal tenderness grows thin.

sentences.zh: 凶儉之年，民輕違犯，可緩其使役，急其禁令。

translations.literal: In years of famine and scarcity, the people lightly violate laws. Corvee labor may be relaxed and prohibitions urgently enforced.
translations.idiomatic: In years of famine and scarcity, the people lightly violate laws. Corvee labor may be relaxed and prohibitions urgently enforced.

sentences.zh: 宜於未然之前，申敕外牧。

translations.literal: It is fitting, before things have happened, to issue edicts to the outer governors.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting, before things have happened, to issue edicts to the outer governors.

sentences.zh: 又一夫幽枉，王道為虧，京師之獄，或恐未盡。

translations.literal: Moreover, when one man is wrongfully imprisoned, the way of kings is impaired; the prisons of the capital may perhaps not yet be fully cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when one man is wrongfully imprisoned, the way of kings is impaired; the prisons of the capital may perhaps not yet be fully cleared.

sentences.zh: 可集見囚於都曹，使明折庶獄者，重加究察。

translations.literal: Gather the prisoners now held in the capital office and have those who clearly judge the multitude of cases examine them again with added scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Gather the prisoners now held in the capital office and have those who clearly judge the multitude of cases examine them again with added scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 輕者即可決遣，重者定狀以聞。

translations.literal: Light cases may be decided and dispatched at once; serious cases should have their facts fixed and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Light cases may be decided and dispatched at once; serious cases should have their facts fixed and reported.

sentences.zh: 罷非急之作，放無用之獸。

translations.literal: Stop non-urgent construction and release useless beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Stop non-urgent construction and release useless beasts.

sentences.zh: 此乃救凶之常法，且以見憂於百姓。

translations.literal: These are the regular methods for relieving famine and also show concern for the common people.
translations.idiomatic: These are the regular methods for relieving famine and also show concern for the common people.

sentences.zh: 論語曰：「不患貧而患不安。

translations.literal: The Analects says: 'Do not worry about poverty but worry about lack of peace.'
translations.idiomatic: The Analects says: 'Do not worry about poverty but worry about lack of peace.'

sentences.zh: 」苟安而樂生，雖遭凶年，何傷於民庶也。

translations.literal: If there is peace and the people live contentedly, though a famine year be encountered, what harm will come to the multitude?
translations.idiomatic: If there is peace and the people live contentedly, though a famine year be encountered, what harm will come to the multitude?

sentences.zh: 愚臣所見，如此而已。

translations.literal: What your foolish servant sees is no more than this.
translations.idiomatic: What your foolish servant sees is no more than this.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「省表聞之，當敕有司依此施行。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Having read your memorial, the relevant offices shall be ordered to implement this."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Having read your memorial, the relevant offices shall be ordered to implement this."

sentences.zh: 後詔閭與太常採雅樂以營金石，又領廣陵王師。

translations.literal: Later Lu was ordered together with the Minister of Ceremonies to collect elegant music for bell and stone instruments, and also to serve as tutor to the Prince of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Later Gao Lu was ordered together with the Minister of Ceremonies to collect elegant music for bell and stone instruments, and also to serve as tutor to the Prince of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 出除鎮南將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out and appointed General Who Guards the South and Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out and appointed General Who Guards the South and Governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 以參定律令之勤，賜布帛千匹、粟一千斛、牛馬各三。

translations.literal: For his diligence in participating in fixing the laws and regulations, he was granted a thousand bolts of silk and cloth, a thousand hu of grain, three oxen, and three horses each.
translations.idiomatic: For his diligence in participating in fixing the laws and regulations, he was granted a thousand bolts of silk and cloth, a thousand hu of grain, three oxen, and three horses each.

sentences.zh: 閭上疏陳伐吳之策，高祖納之。

translations.literal: Lu submitted a memorial setting forth a strategy for campaigning against Wu, and Emperor Xiaowen accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu submitted a memorial setting forth a strategy for campaigning against Wu, and Emperor Xiaowen accepted it.

sentences.zh: 遷都洛陽，閭表諫，言遷有十損，必不獲已，請遷於鄴。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved to Luoyang, Lu submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying the move had ten harms; if it could not be avoided, he asked that the move be to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was moved to Luoyang, Gao Lu submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying the move had ten harms; if it could not be avoided, he asked that the move be to Ye.

sentences.zh: 高祖頗嫌之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen was somewhat displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen was somewhat displeased.

sentences.zh: 蕭鸞雍州刺史曹虎據襄陽請降，詔劉昶、薛真度等四道南伐，車駕親幸懸瓠。

translations.literal: When Xiao Luan's Governor of Yong Province, Cao Hu, held Xiangyang and requested surrender, an edict ordered Liu Chang, Xue Zhendu, and others on four routes to campaign south, and the emperor personally visited Xuanchi.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Luan's Governor of Yong Province, Cao Hu, held Xiangyang and requested surrender, an edict ordered Liu Chang, Xue Zhendu, and others on four routes to campaign south, and the emperor personally visited Xuanchi.

sentences.zh: 閭表諫曰：「洛陽草創，虎既不遣質任，必非誠心，無宜輕舉。

translations.literal: Lu submitted a memorial of remonstrance saying: "Luoyang is newly founded. Since Hu has not sent hostages as pledge, he is surely not sincere—it is not fitting to act lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu submitted a memorial of remonstrance saying: "Luoyang is newly founded. Since Hu has not sent hostages as pledge, he is surely not sincere—it is not fitting to act lightly."

sentences.zh: 」高祖不納。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 虎果虛詐，諸將皆無功而還。

translations.literal: Hu indeed proved false, and the generals all returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Hu indeed proved false, and the generals all returned without achievement.

sentences.zh: 高祖攻鍾離未克，將於淮南修故城而置鎮戍，以撫新附之民，賜閭璽書，具論其狀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen had not yet taken Zhongli and planned to repair old cities in Huainan and establish garrison posts to pacify the newly submitted people, he granted Lu an imperial letter fully explaining the situation.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen had not yet taken Zhongli and planned to repair old cities in Huainan and establish garrison posts to pacify the newly submitted people, he granted Gao Lu an imperial letter fully explaining the situation.

sentences.zh: 閭表曰：「南土亂亡，僭主屢易，陛下命將親征，威陵江左，望風慕化，克拔數城，施恩布德，攜民襁負，可謂澤流邊方，威惠普著矣。

translations.literal: Lu submitted a memorial saying: "The southern lands are in turmoil and ruin; usurping rulers change repeatedly. Your Majesty ordered generals on a personal campaign, your might overshadowing the lands south of the Yangtze. Those who saw the wind and admired your transformation had several cities taken. Bestowing grace and spreading virtue, the people came carrying infants on their backs—this may be called bounty flowing to the border and widespread majestic kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu submitted a memorial saying: "The southern lands are in turmoil and ruin; usurping rulers change repeatedly. Your Majesty ordered generals on a personal campaign, your might overshadowing the lands south of the Yangtze. Those who saw the wind and admired your transformation had several cities taken. Bestowing grace and spreading virtue, the people came carrying infants on their backs—this may be called bounty flowing to the border and widespread majestic kindness.

sentences.zh: 然元非大舉，軍興後時；

translations.literal: Yet originally this was not a great mobilization, and the army was raised late;
translations.idiomatic: Yet originally this was not a great mobilization, and the army was raised late;

sentences.zh: 本為迎降，戎卒實少。

translations.literal: the purpose was to welcome surrender, and the campaigning soldiers were truly few.
translations.idiomatic: the purpose was to welcome surrender, and the campaigning soldiers were truly few.

sentences.zh: 兵法：十則圍之，倍則攻之。

translations.literal: The Art of War says: with tenfold strength, surround; with twofold strength, attack.
translations.idiomatic: The Art of War says: with tenfold strength, surround; with twofold strength, attack.

sentences.zh: 所率既寡，東西懸闊，難以並稱。

translations.literal: What you lead is few, and east and west are far apart—hard to speak of both at once.
translations.idiomatic: What you lead is few, and east and west are far apart—hard to speak of both at once.

sentences.zh: 伏承欲留戍淮南，招撫新附。

translations.literal: I humbly hear that you wish to leave garrisons in Huainan to pacify the newly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hear that you wish to leave garrisons in Huainan to pacify the newly submitted.

sentences.zh: 昔世祖以回山倒海之威，步騎數十萬南臨瓜步，諸郡盡降，而盱眙小城，攻而弗克。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Taiwu, with the might of overturning mountains and seas, marched several hundred thousand infantry and cavalry south to Guabu; all the commanderies submitted, yet the small city of Xuyi he attacked and could not take.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Taiwu, with the might of overturning mountains and seas, marched several hundred thousand infantry and cavalry south to Guabu; all the commanderies submitted, yet the small city of Xuyi he attacked and could not take.

sentences.zh: 班師之日，兵不戍一郡，土不闢一廛。

translations.literal: On the day the army withdrew, not one commandery was garrisoned, not one hamlet opened.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the army withdrew, not one commandery was garrisoned, not one hamlet opened.

sentences.zh: 夫豈無人，以大鎮未平，不可守小故也。

translations.literal: Was it that there were no men? It was because the great garrisons were not pacified and small ones could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: Was it that there were no men? It was because the great garrisons were not pacified and small ones could not be held.

sentences.zh: 堰水先塞其源，伐木必拔其本。

translations.literal: Damming water, first block the source; felling trees, first uproot the root.
translations.idiomatic: Damming water, first block the source; felling trees, first uproot the root.

sentences.zh: 源不塞，本不拔，雖翦枝竭流，終不可絕矣。

translations.literal: If the source is not blocked and the root not uprooted, though branches are cut and streams exhausted, in the end it cannot be ended.
translations.idiomatic: If the source is not blocked and the root not uprooted, though branches are cut and streams exhausted, in the end it cannot be ended.

sentences.zh: 壽陽、盱眙、淮陰，淮南之源本也。

translations.literal: Shouyang, Xuyi, and Huaiyin are the source and root of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyang, Xuyi, and Huaiyin are the source and root of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 三鎮不克其一，而留兵守郡，不可自全明矣。

translations.literal: If not one of the three garrisons is taken, yet troops are left to hold commanderies, self-preservation is clearly impossible.
translations.idiomatic: If not one of the three garrisons is taken, yet troops are left to hold commanderies, self-preservation is clearly impossible.

sentences.zh: 既逼敵之大鎮，隔深淮之險，少置兵不足以自固，多留眾糧運難可充。

translations.literal: Pressed by the enemy's great garrisons and separated by the deep peril of the Huai, too few troops cannot preserve themselves, and too many left behind cannot be supplied with grain.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by the enemy's great garrisons and separated by the deep peril of the Huai, too few troops cannot preserve themselves, and too many left behind cannot be supplied with grain.

sentences.zh: 又欲修渠通漕，路必由于泗口；

translations.literal: If you also wish to repair canals for transport, the route must pass through Sikou;
translations.idiomatic: If you also wish to repair canals for transport, the route must pass through Sikou;

sentences.zh: 泝淮而上，須經角城。

translations.literal: going upstream on the Huai, one must pass Jiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: going upstream on the Huai, one must pass Jiaocheng.

sentences.zh: 淮陰大鎮，舟船素畜，敵因先積之資，以拒始行之路。

translations.literal: Huaiyin is a great garrison where boats and ships are always stored; the enemy, relying on accumulated resources, will resist the route just opened.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyin is a great garrison where boats and ships are always stored; the enemy, relying on accumulated resources, will resist the route just opened.

sentences.zh: 若元戎旋旆，兵士挫怯，夏雨水長，救援實難。

translations.literal: If the main army turns its banners homeward, the soldiers' spirits will be broken and timid; summer rains will swell the waters, and rescue will truly be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: If the main army turns its banners homeward, the soldiers' spirits will be broken and timid; summer rains will swell the waters, and rescue will truly be difficult.

sentences.zh: 忠勇雖奮，事不可濟。

translations.literal: Though loyalty and courage blaze, the affair cannot succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Though loyalty and courage blaze, the affair cannot succeed.

sentences.zh: 淮陰東接山陽，南通江表，兼近江都、海西之資，西有盱眙、壽陽之鎮。

translations.literal: Huaiyin connects east with Shanyang, south with the lands beyond the Yangtze, and is near the resources of Jiangdu and Haixi; west are the garrisons of Xuyi and Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyin connects east with Shanyang, south with the lands beyond the Yangtze, and is near the resources of Jiangdu and Haixi; west are the garrisons of Xuyi and Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 且安土樂本，人之常情，若必留戍，軍還之後，恐為敵擒。

translations.literal: Moreover, contentment with one's land and joy in one's roots is the constant feeling of men. If garrisons must be left, after the army returns I fear they will be captured by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, contentment with one's land and joy in one's roots is the constant feeling of men. If garrisons must be left, after the army returns I fear they will be captured by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 鎮戍新立，懸在異境，以勞禦逸，以新擊舊，而能自固者，未之有也。

translations.literal: Garrison posts newly established, suspended in alien territory—to use the weary against the rested and the new against the old, and yet be able to preserve themselves: never has such a thing occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison posts newly established, suspended in alien territory—to use the weary against the rested and the new against the old, and yet be able to preserve themselves: never has such a thing occurred.

sentences.zh: 昔彭城之役，既克其城，戍鎮已定，而思叛外向者猶過數方。

translations.literal: In the Pengcheng campaign, though the city was taken and garrisons fixed, those who still thought of rebelling and turning outward numbered more than several groups.
translations.idiomatic: In the Pengcheng campaign, though the city was taken and garrisons fixed, those who still thought of rebelling and turning outward numbered more than several groups.

sentences.zh: 角城蕞爾，處在淮北，去淮陽十八里，五固之役，攻圍歷時，卒不能克。

translations.literal: Jiaocheng is tiny, situated north of the Huai, eighteen li from Huaiyin; in the Wugu campaign, attack and siege lasted through the seasons, yet in the end it could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaocheng is tiny, situated north of the Huai, eighteen li from Huaiyin; in the Wugu campaign, attack and siege lasted through the seasons, yet in the end it could not be taken.

sentences.zh: 以今比昔，事兼數倍。

translations.literal: Compared with today, the affair is several times greater.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with today, the affair is several times greater.

sentences.zh: 今以向熱，水雨方降，兵刃既交，難以恩恤。

translations.literal: Now heat is coming, rains are falling, and once arms are crossed, benevolent comfort is hard to extend.
translations.idiomatic: Now heat is coming, rains are falling, and once arms are crossed, benevolent comfort is hard to extend.

sentences.zh: 降附之民及諸守令，亦可徙置淮北。

translations.literal: The submitted people and all defending officials may also be relocated to north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: The submitted people and all defending officials may also be relocated to north of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 如其不然，進兵臨淮，速渡士卒，班師還京。

translations.literal: If not, advance the army to the Huai, quickly cross the soldiers, withdraw the army and return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: If not, advance the army to the Huai, quickly cross the soldiers, withdraw the army and return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 踵太武之成規，營皇居於伊洛。

translations.literal: Follow Emperor Taiwu's established plan and build the imperial residence at Yiluo.
translations.idiomatic: Follow Emperor Taiwu's established plan and build the imperial residence at Yiluo.

sentences.zh: 畜力以待敵釁，布德以懷遠人，使中國清穆，化被遐裔。

translations.literal: Store strength to await the enemy's provocation; spread virtue to win distant peoples—let the Middle Kingdom be clear and tranquil and transformation reach remote regions.
translations.idiomatic: Store strength to await the enemy's provocation; spread virtue to win distant peoples—let the Middle Kingdom be clear and tranquil and transformation reach remote regions.

sentences.zh: 淮南之鎮，自効可期；

translations.literal: The garrisons of Huainan will submit of themselves in due time;
translations.idiomatic: The garrisons of Huainan will submit of themselves in due time;

sentences.zh: 天安之捷，指辰不遠。」

translations.literal: the victory of pacifying Heaven can be expected within the appointed day."
translations.idiomatic: the victory of pacifying Heaven can be expected within the appointed day."

sentences.zh: 車駕還幸石濟，閭朝於行宮。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned and visited Shiji, Lu attended audience at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage returned and visited Shiji, Gao Lu attended audience at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂閭曰：「朕往年之意，不欲決征，但兵士已集，恐為幽王之失，不容中止。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen said to Lu: "In former years I did not wish to decide on a campaign, but the soldiers were already assembled and I feared the error of King You of Zhou—I could not stop midway.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said to Gao Lu: "In former years I did not wish to decide on a campaign, but the soldiers were already assembled and I feared the error of King You of Zhou—I could not stop midway.

sentences.zh: 發洛之日，正欲至於懸瓠，以觀形勢。

translations.literal: On the day we set out from Luoyang, I intended only to reach Xuanchi and observe the situation.
translations.idiomatic: On the day we set out from Luoyang, I intended only to reach Xuanchi and observe the situation.

sentences.zh: 然機不可失，遂至淮南。

translations.literal: But the opportunity could not be lost, and so we reached Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: But the opportunity could not be lost, and so we reached Huainan.

sentences.zh: 而彼諸將，並列州鎮，至無所獲，定由晚一月日故也。

translations.literal: Yet those generals, each holding provincial garrisons, ultimately gained nothing—it was surely because we were a month late.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those generals, each holding provincial garrisons, ultimately gained nothing—it was surely because we were a month late.

sentences.zh: 」閭對曰：「人皆是其所事，而非其所不事，猶犬之吠非其主。

translations.literal: Lu replied: "Men all bark at what they serve and not at what they do not serve—it is like a dog barking at someone who is not its master.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu replied: "Men all bark at what they serve and not at what they do not serve—it is like a dog barking at someone who is not its master.

sentences.zh: 且古者攻戰之法，倍則攻之，十則圍之。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the methods of attack and battle of antiquity: with twofold strength, attack; with tenfold strength, surround.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the methods of attack and battle of antiquity: with twofold strength, attack; with tenfold strength, surround.

sentences.zh: 聖駕親戎，誠應大捷，所以無大獲者，良由兵少故也。

translations.literal: When the sacred carriage campaigns in person, there should indeed be a great victory; the reason there was no great gain was truly because the troops were few.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacred carriage campaigns in person, there should indeed be a great victory; the reason there was no great gain was truly because the troops were few.

sentences.zh: 且徙都者，天下之大事，今京邑甫爾，庶事造創，臣聞詩云：『惠此中國，以綏四方。

translations.literal: Moreover, moving the capital is a great affair of the realm. Now the capital has only just been established and the multitude of affairs are newly created. I hear the Odes say: 'Be kind to this central state to pacify the four quarters.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, moving the capital is a great affair of the realm. Now the capital has only just been established and the multitude of affairs are newly created. I hear the Odes say: 'Be kind to this central state to pacify the four quarters.'

sentences.zh: 』臣願陛下從容伊瀍，優遊京洛，使德被四海，中國緝寧，然後向化之徒，自然樂附。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes that Your Majesty would take leisure at the Yi and Luo, enjoying ease in the capital of Luoyang, so that virtue covers the four seas, the Middle Kingdom is brought to peace, and then those turning to your transformation will naturally be glad to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant wishes that Your Majesty would take leisure at the Yi and Luo, enjoying ease in the capital of Luoyang, so that virtue covers the four seas, the Middle Kingdom is brought to peace, and then those turning to your transformation will naturally be glad to attach themselves.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「願從容伊瀍，實亦不少，但未獲耳。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen said: "To take leisure at the Yi and Luo is indeed not a little—but it has not yet been obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said: "To take leisure at the Yi and Luo is indeed not a little—but it has not yet been obtained.

sentences.zh: 」閭曰：「司馬相如臨終恨不見封禪。

translations.literal: Lu said: "Sima Xiangru on his deathbed regretted not seeing the feng and shan sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu said: "Sima Xiangru on his deathbed regretted not seeing the feng and shan sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 今雖江介不賓，小賊未殄，然中州之地，略亦盡平，豈可於聖明之辰，而闕盛禮。

translations.literal: Now though the lands beyond the Yangtze are not yet submitted and small bandits are not yet exterminated, the lands of the central provinces are largely pacified—how can one in a sage and enlightened age omit this grand rite?
translations.idiomatic: Now though the lands beyond the Yangtze are not yet submitted and small bandits are not yet exterminated, the lands of the central provinces are largely pacified—how can one in a sage and enlightened age omit this grand rite?

sentences.zh: 齊桓公霸諸侯，猶欲封禪，而況萬乘。

translations.literal: Duke Huan of Qi, though he merely dominated the feudal lords, still wished to perform the feng and shan—how much more so for one who possesses ten thousand chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi, though he merely dominated the feudal lords, still wished to perform the feng and shan—how much more so for one who possesses ten thousand chariots.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「由此桓公屈於管仲。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen said: "Because of this Duke Huan yielded to Guan Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said: "Because of this Duke Huan yielded to Guan Zhong.

sentences.zh: 荊揚未一，豈得如卿言也。

translations.literal: Jing and Yang are not yet unified—how can it be as you say?
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Yang are not yet unified—how can it be as you say?

sentences.zh: 」閭曰：「漢之名臣，皆不以江南為中國。

translations.literal: Lu said: "Among the famous ministers of Han, none took the lands south of the Yangtze as the Middle Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu said: "Among the famous ministers of Han, none took the lands south of the Yangtze as the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 且三代之境，亦不能遠。

translations.literal: Moreover, the domains of the Three Dynasties could not extend far either.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the domains of the Three Dynasties could not extend far either.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「淮海惟揚州，荊及衡陽惟荊州，此非近中國乎？」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen said: "In the Tribute of Yu, the Huai and sea are Yang Province; Jing and Mount Heng are Jing Province—is this not near the Middle Kingdom?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said: "In the Tribute of Yu, the Huai and sea are Yang Province; Jing and Mount Heng are Jing Province—is this not near the Middle Kingdom?"

sentences.zh: 及車駕至鄴，高祖頻幸其州館。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Ye, Emperor Xiaowen frequently visited his provincial residence.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage reached Ye, Emperor Xiaowen frequently visited his provincial residence.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「閭昔在中禁，有定禮正樂之勳；

translations.literal: An edict said: "Lu formerly in the inner palace had the merit of fixing rites and correcting music;
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Gao Lu formerly in the inner palace had the merit of fixing rites and correcting music;

sentences.zh: 作藩於州，有廉清公幹之美。

translations.literal: serving as feudal minister in the province, he had the beauty of upright, incorrupt, and public-spirited competence.
translations.idiomatic: serving as feudal minister in the province, he had the beauty of upright, incorrupt, and public-spirited competence.

sentences.zh: 自大軍停軫，庶事咸豐，可謂國之老成，善始令終者也。

translations.literal: Since the great army halted its wheels, the multitude of affairs have all been abundant—he may be called an elder statesman of the country, one who begins well and ends well.
translations.idiomatic: Since the great army halted its wheels, the multitude of affairs have all been abundant—he may be called an elder statesman of the country, one who begins well and ends well.

sentences.zh: 每惟厥德，朕甚嘉焉。

translations.literal: Constantly reflecting on his virtue, I greatly commend him.
